They do not comprehend or discern, for He has shut their eyes so they cannot see and closed their minds so they cannot understand. (44:18).

And no one considers in his heart, no one has the knowledge or insight to say, “I burned half of it in the fire, and I baked bread on its coals; I roasted meat and I ate. Shall I make something detestable with the rest of it? Shall I bow down to a block of wood?” (44:19).
He feeds on ashes. His deluded heart has led him astray, and he cannot deliver himself or say, “Is not this thing in my right hand a lie?” (44:20).
Remember these things, O Jacob, for you are My servant, O Israel. I have made you, and you are My servant; O Israel, I will never forget you. (44:21).
I have blotted out your transgressions like a cloud, and your sins like a mist. Return to Me, for I have redeemed you. (44:22).

Sing for joy, O heavens, for the LORD has done this; shout aloud, O depths of the earth. Break forth in song, O mountains, you forests and all your trees. For the LORD has redeemed Jacob, and revealed His glory in Israel. (44:23).
Thus says the LORD, your Redeemer who formed you from the womb: “I am the LORD, who has made all things, who alone stretched out the heavens, who by Myself spread out the earth, (44:24).
who foils the signs of false prophets and makes fools of diviners, who confounds the wise and turns their knowledge into nonsense, (44:25).

who confirms the message of His servant and fulfills the counsel of His messengers, who says of Jerusalem, ‘She will be inhabited,’ and of the cities of Judah, ‘They will be rebuilt, and I will restore their ruins,’ (44:26).
who says to the depths of the sea, ‘Be dry, and I will dry up your currents,’ (44:27).
who says of Cyrus, ‘My shepherd will fulfill all that I desire,’ who says of Jerusalem, ‘She will be rebuilt,’ and of the temple, ‘Let its foundation be laid.’” (44:28).
crossRefs: Deuteronomy 6:4: The LORD is one (exclusive claim).
John 7:37-39: Living water and the Spirit.
Psalm 115:4-8: Idol makers become like them.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: מָחָה (maḥah), Greek (LXX): ἐξαλείφω, Aramaic: מחי
translationNotes.note: Erase the record of sins (43:25).

translationNotes.term: I am the first and the last
translationNotes.original: Hebrew: רִאשׁוֹן… אַחֲרוֹן (riʾshon… aḥaron), Greek (LXX): πρῶτος… ἔσχατος, Aramaic: קַדְמָאָה… אַחֲרָאָה
translationNotes.note: Title of unique sovereignty (44:6).

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: אֵפֶר (efer), Greek (LXX): σποδός, Aramaic: אפרא
translationNotes.note: Image for empty trust in idols (44:20).

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: פֶּסֶל (pesel), a carved image
translationNotes.note: Isaiah 44:14-17 follows a single tree from planting to worship, and the joke is in the sequence. The man grows it, cuts it, burns half of it to warm himself and roast his dinner, then carves a god out of what is left and prays to it for salvation. Isaiah 41:7 adds the workshop detail from the other trade: the goldsmith encourages the man with the hammer, and they fasten the finished idol down with nails so it will not topple over. Jeremiah 10:3-5 makes the same point about a figure that has to be carried because it cannot walk.

stories.keyTakeaway: God promises Spirit and redemption, declares there is no other God, and mocks lifeless idols made from the same wood used for cooking.

stories.title: 🪙 Isaiah 45
summaryBullets: This is what the LORD says to Cyrus His anointed, whose right hand I have grasped to subdue nations before him, to disarm kings, to open the doors before him, so that the gates will not be shut: (45:1).
“I will go before you and level the mountains; I will break down the gates of bronze and cut through the bars of iron. (45:2).
I will give you the treasures of darkness and the riches hidden in secret places, so that you may know that I am the LORD, the God of Israel, who calls you by name. (45:3).
For the sake of Jacob My servant and Israel My chosen one, I call you by name; I have given you a title of honor, though you have not known Me. (45:4).
I am the LORD, and there is no other; there is no God but Me. I will equip you for battle, though you have not known Me, (45:5).
so that all may know, from where the sun rises to where it sets, that there is none but Me; I am the LORD, and there is no other. (45:6).
I form the light and create the darkness; I bring prosperity and create calamity. I, the LORD, do all these things. (45:7).
Drip down, O heavens, from above, and let the skies pour down righteousness. Let the earth open up that salvation may sprout and righteousness spring up with it; I, the LORD, have created it. (45:8).
Woe to him who quarrels with his Maker— one clay pot among many. Does the clay ask the potter, ‘What are you making?’ Does your work say, ‘He has no hands’? (45:9).
Woe to him who says to his father, ‘What have you begotten?’ or to his mother, ‘What have you brought forth?’” (45:10).
Thus says the LORD, the Holy One of Israel, and its Maker: “Concerning things to come, do you question Me about My sons, or instruct Me in the work of My hands? (45:11).
It is I who made the earth and created man upon it. It was My hands that stretched out the heavens, and I ordained all their host. (45:12).
I will raise up Cyrus in righteousness, and I will make all his ways straight. He will rebuild My city and set My exiles free, but not for payment or reward, says the LORD of Hosts.” (45:13).

This is what the LORD says: “The products of Egypt and the merchandise of Cush, along with the Sabeans, men of stature, will come over to you and will be yours; they will trudge behind you; they will come over in chains and bow down to you. They will confess to you: ‘God is indeed with you, and there is no other; there is no other God.’” (45:14).
Truly You are a God who hides Himself, O God of Israel, the Savior. (45:15).
They will all be put to shame and humiliated; the makers of idols will depart together in disgrace. (45:16).
But Israel will be saved by the LORD with an everlasting salvation; you will not be put to shame or humiliated, to ages everlasting. (45:17).

For thus says the LORD, who created the heavens— He is God; He formed the earth and fashioned it; He established it; He did not create it to be empty, but formed it to be inhabited: “I am the LORD, and there is no other. (45:18).
I have not spoken in secret, from a place in a land of darkness. I did not say to the descendants of Jacob, ‘Seek Me in a wasteland.’ I, the LORD, speak the truth; I say what is right. (45:19).
Come, gather together, and draw near, you fugitives from the nations. Ignorant are those who carry idols of wood and pray to a god that cannot save. (45:20).

Speak up and present your case— yes, let them take counsel together. Who foretold this long ago? Who announced it from ancient times? Was it not I, the LORD? There is no other God but Me, a righteous God and Savior; there is none but Me. (45:21).
Turn to Me and be saved, all the ends of the earth; for I am God, and there is no other. (45:22).
By Myself I have sworn; truth has gone out from My mouth, a word that will not be revoked: Every knee will bow before Me, every tongue will swear allegiance. (45:23).
Surely they will say of Me, ‘In the LORD alone are righteousness and strength.’” All who rage against Him will come to Him and be put to shame. (45:24).
In the LORD all descendants of Israel will be justified and will exult. (45:25).
crossRefs: Ezra 1:1-4: Cyrus proclaims that the LORD has appointed him to build a house at Jerusalem, and releases the exiles to go up and build it.
2 Chronicles 36:22-23: The same proclamation closes Chronicles, made in the first year of Cyrus to fulfill the word spoken through Jeremiah.
Romans 14:11: Paul quotes Isaiah 45:23, 'every knee will bow before Me; every tongue will confess to God.'
Philippians 2:10-11: At the name of Jesus every knee bows and every tongue confesses that Jesus Christ is Lord.
Jeremiah 27:5-6: The LORD says He made the earth and gives it to whom He pleases, and has handed these lands to Nebuchadnezzar His servant.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: כּוֹרֶשׁ (Koresh), Greek (LXX): Κῦρος, Aramaic: כּוֹרֵשׁ
translationNotes.note: Persian king named as God’s instrument (44:28-45:1).

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: מְשִׁיחוֹ (meshicho), Greek (LXX): χριστός, Aramaic: מְשִׁיחָא
translationNotes.note: Title used uniquely of a foreign ruler here (45:1).

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: רָע (raʿ, ‘disaster/calamity’), Greek (LXX): κακά, Aramaic: בִּישָׁא
translationNotes.note: 45:7 states God brings disaster/judgment; it does not mean God commits moral evil.

translationNotes.term: Cyrus and the policy of sending people home
translationNotes.original: Hebrew: כּוֹרֶשׁ (Koresh) - Old Persian: Kurush
translationNotes.note: Cyrus took Babylon in 539 BC and reversed the Assyrian and Babylonian practice of breaking nations by deporting them. A clay barrel found in the ruins of Babylon in 1879 and now in the British Museum, called the Cyrus Cylinder, has him record returning gods to their own sanctuaries and settling displaced peoples back in their own cities. Ezra 1:1-4 records the decree that sent Judah home to rebuild the temple, and Isaiah 44:28 and 45:1 name Cyrus and give him the title anointed, the only foreign king in Scripture called that.

stories.keyTakeaway: The LORD addresses Cyrus by name, promising to subdue nations before him and rebuild Jerusalem and free the exiles; the LORD declares his singular supremacy over all creation and calls the ends of the earth to turn and be saved, warning that all who oppose him will be put to shame.

stories.title: 🪙 Isaiah 46
summaryBullets: Bel crouches; Nebo cowers. Their idols weigh down beasts and cattle. The images you carry are burdensome, a load to the weary animal. (46:1).
The gods cower; they crouch together, unable to relieve the burden; but they themselves go into captivity. (46:2).
“Listen to Me, O house of Jacob, all the remnant of the house of Israel, who have been sustained from the womb, carried along since birth. (46:3).
Even to your old age, I will be the same, and I will bear you up when you turn gray. I have made you, and I will carry you; I will sustain you and deliver you. (46:4).
To whom will you liken Me or count Me equal? To whom will you compare Me, that we should be alike? (46:5).
They pour out their bags of gold and weigh out silver on scales; they hire a goldsmith to fashion it into a god, so they can bow down and worship. (46:6).

They lift it to their shoulder and carry it along; they set it in its place, and there it stands, not budging from that spot. They cry out to it, but it does not answer; it saves no one from his troubles. (46:7).
Remember this and be brave; take it to heart, you transgressors! (46:8).
Remember what happened long ago, for I am God, and there is no other; I am God, and there is none like Me. (46:9).
I declare the end from the beginning, and from ancient times what is still to come. I say, ‘My purpose will stand, and all My good pleasure I will accomplish.’ (46:10).
I summon a bird of prey from the east, a man for My purpose from a far-off land. Truly I have spoken, and truly I will bring it to pass. I have planned it, and I will surely do it. (46:11).
Listen to Me, you stubborn people, far removed from righteousness: (46:12).
I am bringing My righteousness near; it is not far away, and My salvation will not be delayed. I will grant salvation to Zion and adorn Israel with My splendor. (46:13).
crossRefs: Jeremiah 50:2: The announcement that Babylon is captured, Bel put to shame, Marduk shattered, and her images disgraced.
Jeremiah 51:44: The LORD says He will punish Bel in Babylon and make him spew out what he swallowed, and the wall of Babylon will fall.
Isaiah 44:9-20: The craftsman burns half his log for warmth and bakes bread over it, then carves a god from the rest and bows down to it.
Deuteronomy 32:11-12: The LORD is the eagle who spreads His wings, catches His young, and carries them on His pinions.
Psalm 115:4-8: Idols of silver and gold have mouths that cannot speak, eyes that cannot see, and feet that cannot walk.

translationNotes.term: Bel and Nebo carried out on carts
translationNotes.original: Hebrew: בֵּל (Bel) - נְבוֹ (Nevo)
translationNotes.note: Bel is a title meaning lord and it belonged to Marduk, the chief god of Babylon; Nebo is Nabu, his son, the god of writing and scribes, whose temple stood at nearby Borsippa. Their names are all over Babylonian personal names, Nebuchadnezzar and Belshazzar among them. Once a year at the New Year festival the images were carried in procession through the city, which is exactly the picture Isaiah 46:1-2 turns inside out: the statues that were paraded in triumph are now loaded on pack animals as loot, dead weight on a tired beast, going into captivity themselves.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: עָמַס (amas, to load up) - סָבַל (saval, to bear a burden)
translationNotes.note: The chapter turns on one verb used both ways. At 46:1 the idols are a load strapped to tired animals, and at 46:7 men lift the god on their shoulders, set it down, and it stands there and cannot move from its place. Against that, 46:3-4 has God carrying Israel from the womb to grey hair. One side is carried and one side carries, and the chapter says nothing else until 46:5 asks who you would compare him to.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: צוֹרֵף (tsoreph, refiner or goldsmith)
translationNotes.note: 46:6 walks through the making of a god as a transaction: gold poured out of the purse, silver weighed on the balance, a craftsman hired, and then the buyers fall down before the thing they have just paid for. Silver was weighed rather than counted because coinage was not yet in use, so the scales in this verse are the ordinary equipment of a market stall.

translationNotes.term: A bird of prey from the east
translationNotes.original: Hebrew: עַיִט (ayit, bird of prey)
translationNotes.note: 46:11 calls a man from a far country the way a falconer calls a bird, and an ayit is a raptor, the same word for the birds that came down on Abram's carcasses at Genesis 15:11. The line pairs the speed of the call with the claim in 46:10, declaring the end from the beginning, and 46:13 says the deliverance is not far off.

stories.keyTakeaway: The gods Bel and Nebo are carried away as burdens while Isaiah contrasts them with God, who has sustained Jacob since birth and will carry them to old age; God declares his uniqueness, announces his coming purposes through a summoned ruler from the east, and promises righteousness and salvation to Zion.

stories.title: 🪙 Isaiah 47
summaryBullets: “Go down and sit in the dust, O Virgin Daughter of Babylon. Sit on the ground without a throne, O Daughter of the Chaldeans! For you will no longer be called tender or delicate. (47:1).
Take millstones and grind flour; remove your veil; strip off your skirt, bare your thigh, and wade through the streams. (47:2).
Your nakedness will be uncovered and your shame will be exposed. I will take vengeance; I will spare no one.” (47:3).
Our Redeemer — the LORD of Hosts is His name — is the Holy One of Israel. (47:4).
“Sit in silence and go into darkness, O Daughter of the Chaldeans. For you will no longer be called the queen of kingdoms. (47:5).
I was angry with My people; I profaned My heritage, and I placed them under your control. You showed them no mercy; even on the elderly you laid a most heavy yoke. (47:6).
You said, ‘I will be queen forever.’ You did not take these things to heart or consider their outcome. (47:7).
So now hear this, O lover of luxury who sits securely, who says to herself, ‘I am, and there is none besides me. I will never be a widow or know the loss of children.’ (47:8).

These two things will overtake you in a moment, in a single day: loss of children, and widowhood. They will come upon you in full measure, in spite of your many sorceries and the potency of your spells. (47:9).
You were secure in your wickedness; you said, ‘No one sees me.’ Your wisdom and knowledge led you astray; you told yourself, ‘I am, and there is none besides me.’ (47:10).

But disaster will come upon you; you will not know how to charm it away. A calamity will befall you that you will be unable to ward off. Devastation will happen to you suddenly and unexpectedly. (47:11).
So take your stand with your spells and with your many sorceries, with which you have wearied yourself from your youth. Perhaps you will succeed; perhaps you will inspire terror! (47:12).
You are wearied by your many counselors; let them come forward now and save you— your astrologers who observe the stars, who monthly predict your fate. (47:13).
Surely they are like stubble; the fire will burn them up. They cannot deliver themselves from the power of the flame. There will be no coals to warm them or fire to sit beside. (47:14).
This is what they are to you — those with whom you have labored and traded from youth— each one strays in his own direction; not one of them can save you. (47:15).
crossRefs: Revelation 18:7-8: Babylon says in her heart, 'I sit as queen; I am not a widow,' and her plagues come in one day.
Daniel 5:7-8: Belshazzar summons the enchanters, astrologers, and diviners of Babylon, and not one of them can read the writing.
Deuteronomy 18:10-12: Divination, sorcery, spells, and consulting the dead are named as detestable practices the LORD drives nations out for.
Judges 16:21: The Philistines blind Samson, bind him with bronze shackles, and set him to grinding grain in the prison.
Isaiah 13:19-22: Babylon, the jewel of the kingdoms, is overthrown like Sodom and Gomorrah and left to desert creatures and jackals.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: רֵחַיִם (rechayim)
translationNotes.note: A household mill was two stones, a fixed lower one and an upper one turned by hand, and grinding the day's grain was the longest and lowest job in the house, given to slave women. The blinded Samson was set to grind in the Gaza prison (Judges 16:21), and Deuteronomy 24:6 forbids taking a millstone in pledge because that seizes a family's food supply. Verse 2 puts the queen of kingdoms at the handmill.

translationNotes.term: Remove your veil, bare your thigh
translationNotes.original: Hebrew: גַּלִּי־שֹׁבֶל (galli shovel)
translationNotes.note: This is how prisoners of war were driven into exile. Isaiah 20:4 states it plainly: the king of Assyria leads Egyptian and Cushite captives away naked and barefoot with their buttocks uncovered. Wading the streams means fording rivers on foot with skirts hitched up, in full view, on the long march to the conqueror's land.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: כַּשְׂדִּים (Kasdim)
translationNotes.note: The Chaldeans were a people of southern Babylonia whose dynasty took the Babylonian throne under Nabopolassar in 626 BC. His son Nebuchadnezzar II broke Egypt at Carchemish, took Jerusalem, and burned the temple in 586 BC. By Daniel's day the same word also names a class of court diviners at the king's table (Daniel 2:2).

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: הֹבְרֵי שָׁמַיִם (hovrei shamayim)
translationNotes.note: Babylon ran celestial divination as a state service. Trained scribes watched the moon, the planets, and eclipses month by month, matched what they saw against long written omen collections, and sent reports to the king telling him what was coming. Daniel 2:2 lists that whole guild, and Deuteronomy 18:10-12 forbids Israel to use any of it.

translationNotes.term: I am, and there is none besides me
translationNotes.original: Hebrew: אֲנִי וְאַפְסִי עוֹד (ani ve-afsi od)
translationNotes.note: Babylon is quoted saying about herself the exact thing the LORD says about Himself elsewhere in this book: I am the LORD, and there is no other, besides Me there is no God (45:5-6, 45:18, 45:21-22, 46:9). She says it twice, in verses 8 and 10.

stories.keyTakeaway: God commands Babylon to be humbled and stripped of its power; the city trusted in its own permanence, sorcery, and astrologers, but disaster will overtake it in a moment and none of its magic or counsel can prevent it.

stories.title: 🪙 Isaiah 48
summaryBullets: “Listen to this, O house of Jacob, you who are called by the name of Israel, who have descended from the line of Judah, who swear by the name of the LORD, who invoke the God of Israel — but not in truth or righteousness — (48:1).
who indeed call yourselves after the holy city and lean on the God of Israel; the LORD of Hosts is His name. (48:2).
I foretold the former things long ago; they came out of My mouth and I proclaimed them. Suddenly I acted, and they came to pass. (48:3).
For I knew that you are stubborn; your neck is iron and your forehead is bronze. (48:4).
Therefore I declared it to you long ago; I announced it before it came to pass, so that you could not claim, ‘My idol has done this; my carved image and molten god has ordained it.’ (48:5).
You have heard these things; look at them all. Will you not acknowledge them? From now on I will tell you of new things, hidden things unknown to you. (48:6).
They are created now, and not long ago; you have not heard of them before today. So you cannot claim, ‘I already knew them!’ (48:7).
You have never heard; you have never understood; for a long time your ears have not been open. For I knew how deceitful you are; you have been called a rebel from birth. (48:8).
For the sake of My name I will delay My wrath; for the sake of My praise I will restrain it, so that you will not be cut off. (48:9).
See, I have refined you, but not as silver; I have tested you in the furnace of affliction. (48:10).
For My own sake, My very own sake, I will act; for how can I let Myself be defamed? I will not yield My glory to another. (48:11).
Listen to Me, O Jacob, and Israel, whom I have called: I am He; I am the first, and I am the last. (48:12).
Surely My own hand founded the earth, and My right hand spread out the heavens; when I summon them, they stand up together. (48:13).

Come together, all of you, and listen: Which of the idols has foretold these things? The LORD’s chosen ally will carry out His desire against Babylon, and His arm will be against the Chaldeans. (48:14).
I, even I, have spoken; yes, I have called him. I have brought him, and he will succeed in his mission. (48:15).
Come near to Me and listen to this: From the beginning I have not spoken in secret; from the time it happened, I was there.” And now the Lord GOD has sent me, accompanied by His Spirit. (48:16).
Thus says the LORD your Redeemer, the Holy One of Israel: “I am the LORD your God, who teaches you for your benefit, who directs you in the way you should go. (48:17).
If only you had paid attention to My commandments, your peace would have been like a river, and your righteousness like waves of the sea. (48:18).
Your descendants would have been as countless as the sand, and your offspring as numerous as its grains; their name would never be cut off or eliminated from My presence.” (48:19).
Leave Babylon! Flee from the Chaldeans! Declare it with a shout of joy, proclaim it, let it go out to the ends of the earth, saying, “The LORD has redeemed His servant Jacob!” (48:20).
They did not thirst when He led them through the deserts; He made water flow for them from the rock; He split the rock, and water gushed out. (48:21).
“There is no peace,” says the LORD, “for the wicked.” (48:22).
crossRefs: Revelation 18:4: A voice from heaven says, 'Come out of her, My people, so that you will not share in her sins.'
Jeremiah 51:6: 'Flee from Babylon! Escape with your lives!' because the time of the LORD's vengeance has come.
Deuteronomy 4:20: The LORD brought Israel out of the iron furnace, out of Egypt, to be the people of His inheritance.
Exodus 17:5-6: Moses strikes the rock at Horeb with his staff and water comes out of it for the people to drink.
Isaiah 57:21: The same refrain closes the next section of the book: 'There is no peace,' says my God, 'for the wicked.'

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: מִמֵּי יְהוּדָה (mi-mey Yehudah)
translationNotes.note: The Hebrew literally says out of the waters of Judah. It is a plain figure for a man's seed and so for physical descent, which is why English versions render it line or loins. The verse is telling people who claim the pedigree that the pedigree is all they have.

translationNotes.term: Swear by the name of the LORD
translationNotes.original: Hebrew: הַנִּשְׁבָּעִים בְּשֵׁם יְהוָה (ha-nishbaim be-shem YHWH)
translationNotes.note: An oath put the swearer under the authority of the one he swore by and invited that one to act if he lied. Deuteronomy 6:13 requires that Israel swear by the LORD's name and no other, and Leviticus 19:12 makes swearing falsely by it a profaning of the name itself. Verse 1 says they do it, but not in truth.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: כּוּר עֹנִי (kur oni)
translationNotes.note: A kur is a smelting furnace, where ore is heated until the metal separates from the rock. Deuteronomy 4:20 and 1 Kings 8:51 call Egypt an iron kur, the furnace Israel was brought out of. Verse 10 says the refining this time was not the silver kind, which is done for the purity of the metal, but the affliction kind.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: כּוֹרֶשׁ (Koresh)
translationNotes.note: The man is named earlier in the book: Cyrus, king of Persia (44:28; 45:1). Cyrus took Babylon in 539 BC and the next year issued the decree that let deported peoples go home, which Ezra 1:1-4 records for Judah. The Cyrus Cylinder, a clay barrel inscription from Babylon now in the British Museum, states the same policy of returning captive peoples and their gods to their own cities.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: בָּקַע צוּר (baqa tsur)
translationNotes.note: Verse 21 is not a new promise but a citation of the wilderness. Exodus 17:6 has Moses striking the rock at Horeb and water coming out for the whole camp, and Numbers 20:11 repeats it at Meribah. The prophet is telling people leaving Babylon that the road home has the same precedent behind it.

stories.keyTakeaway: God addresses the stubborn descendants of Jacob, reminding them he announced events long ago so they could not credit their idols; he declares he will now reveal new things and promises to guide them to peace if they obey, while warning that the wicked will find no peace.

stories.title: 🕯️ Isaiah 49
summaryBullets: Listen to Me, O islands; pay attention, O distant peoples: The LORD called Me from the womb; from the body of My mother He named Me. (49:1).
He made My mouth like a sharp sword; He hid Me in the shadow of His hand. He made Me like a polished arrow; He hid Me in His quiver. (49:2).
He said to Me, “You are My Servant, Israel, in whom I will display My glory.” (49:3).
But I said, “I have labored in vain, I have spent My strength in futility and vanity; yet My vindication is with the LORD, and My reward is with My God.” (49:4).

And now says the LORD, who formed Me from the womb to be His Servant, to bring Jacob back to Him, that Israel might be gathered to Him— for I am honored in the sight of the LORD, and My God is My strength— (49:5).

He says: “It is not enough for You to be My Servant, to raise up the tribes of Jacob, and to restore the protected ones of Israel. I will also make You a light for the nations, to bring My salvation to the ends of the earth.” (49:6).

Thus says the LORD, the Redeemer and Holy One of Israel, to Him who was despised and abhorred by the nation, to the Servant of rulers: “Kings will see You and rise, and princes will bow down, because of the LORD, who is faithful, the Holy One of Israel, who has chosen You.” (49:7).

This is what the LORD says: “In the time of favor I will answer You, and in the day of salvation I will help You; I will keep You and appoint You to be a covenant for the people, to restore the land, to apportion its desolate inheritances, (49:8).
to say to the prisoners, ‘Come out,’ and to those in darkness, ‘Show yourselves.’ They will feed along the pathways, and find pasture on every barren hill. (49:9).
They will not hunger or thirst, nor will scorching heat or sun beat down on them. For He who has compassion on them will guide them and lead them beside springs of water. (49:10).
I will turn all My mountains into roads, and My highways will be raised up. (49:11).
Behold, they will come from far away, from the north and from the west, and from the land of Aswan.” (49:12).
Shout for joy, O heavens; rejoice, O earth; break forth in song, O mountains! For the LORD has comforted His people, and He will have compassion on His afflicted ones. (49:13).
But Zion said, “The LORD has forsaken me; the Lord has forgotten me!” (49:14).
“Can a woman forget her nursing child, or lack compassion for the son of her womb? Even if she could forget, I will not forget you! (49:15).
Behold, I have inscribed you on the palms of My hands; your walls are ever before Me. (49:16).
Your builders hasten back; your destroyers and wreckers depart from you. (49:17).
Lift up your eyes and look around. They all gather together; they come to you. As surely as I live,” declares the LORD, “you will wear them all as jewelry and put them on like a bride. (49:18).
For your ruined and desolate places and your ravaged land will now indeed be too small for your people, and those who devoured you will be far away. (49:19).
Yet the children of your bereavement will say in your hearing, ‘This place is too small for us; make room for us to live here.’ (49:20).

Then you will say in your heart, ‘Who has begotten these for me? I was bereaved and barren; I was exiled and rejected. So who has reared them? Look, I was left all alone, so where did they come from?’” (49:21).

This is what the Lord GOD says: “Behold, I will lift up My hand to the nations, and raise My banner to the peoples. They will bring your sons in their arms and carry your daughters on their shoulders. (49:22).

Kings will be your foster fathers, and their queens your nursing mothers. They will bow to you facedown and lick the dust at your feet. Then you will know that I am the LORD; those who hope in Me will never be put to shame.” (49:23).
Can the plunder be snatched from the mighty, or the captives of a tyrant be delivered? (49:24).

Indeed, this is what the LORD says: “Even the captives of the mighty will be taken away, and the plunder of the tyrant will be retrieved; I will contend with those who contend with you, and I will save your children. (49:25).

I will make your oppressors eat their own flesh; they will be drunk on their own blood, as with wine. Then all mankind will know that I, the LORD, am your Savior and your Redeemer, the Mighty One of Jacob.” (49:26).
crossRefs: Luke 2:30-32: Simeon holds the child and calls Him a light for revelation to the Gentiles and for glory to God's people Israel.
Acts 13:47: Paul and Barnabas take the commission as their own: 'I have made you a light for the Gentiles, to bring salvation to the ends of the earth.'
2 Corinthians 6:2: Paul quotes Isaiah 49:8, 'In the time of favor I heard you, and in the day of salvation I helped you.'
Jeremiah 1:5: 'Before I formed you in the womb I knew you, and before you were born I set you apart and appointed you as a prophet.'
Revelation 7:16: Never again will they hunger or thirst, nor will the sun beat down on them or any scorching heat.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: חַקֹּתִיךְ עַל־כַּפָּיִם (ḥaqqotikh ʿal-kappayim), Greek (LXX): ἐζωγράφηκά σε ἐπὶ τῶν χειρῶν, Aramaic: רְשִׁימְתִּיךְ עַל כַּפַּי
translationNotes.note: Image of permanent remembrance (49:16).

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: אוֹר גּוֹיִם (ʾor goyim), Greek (LXX): φῶς ἐθνῶν, Aramaic: נהוֹרָא דַּעַמְמַיָּא
translationNotes.note: Global scope of the Servant’s mission (49:6).

translationNotes.term: A sharp sword and a polished arrow
translationNotes.original: Hebrew: חֵץ בָּרוּר (chets barur, a polished arrow) - בְּאַשְׁפָּתוֹ (be-ashpatho, in his quiver)
translationNotes.note: 49:2 is two weapons and both are being kept back. A blade is stored in shadow so it does not rust or catch the light and give a position away; an arrow is burnished so it flies clean, and then it is put in the quiver rather than shot. The verse says the mouth was made like the sword, so the weapon in question is speech.

translationNotes.term: Kings shall lick the dust of your feet
translationNotes.original: Hebrew: וַעֲפַר רַגְלַיִךְ יְלַחֵכוּ (va-aphar raglayikh yelachekhu)
translationNotes.note: 49:23 uses the required posture of the ancient court, face to the ground before a throne, which Assyrian and Persian palace reliefs show foreign rulers doing. Put beside 49:15, where a nursing mother might forget her child sooner than God forgets, the chapter sets the lowest posture a king could take next to the most ordinary bond there is.

translationNotes.term: Can the prey be taken from the mighty?
translationNotes.original: Hebrew: מַלְקוֹחַ (malqoach, plunder) - שְׁבִי צַדִּיק (shevi tsaddiq, the captive of a righteous one)
translationNotes.note: 49:24-25 uses the law of war as the objection and then overrules it. Plunder belonged to the man who took it and captives belonged to the victor, so getting them back was not a matter of right but of force. The answer at 49:25 does not dispute the rule; it says the captives will be taken back anyway, from the mighty.

stories.keyTakeaway: The servant, called from birth and equipped by the Lord, expresses discouragement but receives reassurance that his mission will extend salvation to the Gentiles and restore scattered Israel. Zion, though feeling abandoned, is promised that the Lord has inscribed her on his palms and will restore her children through the nations as a sign of his power.

headings.text: The Servant and Light to the Gentiles

stories.title: 🕯️ Isaiah 50
summaryBullets: This is what the LORD says: “Where is your mother’s certificate of divorce with which I sent her away? Or to which of My creditors did I sell you? Look, you were sold for your iniquities, and for your transgressions your mother was sent away. (50:1).

Why was no one there when I arrived? Why did no one answer when I called? Is My hand too short to redeem you? Or do I lack the strength to deliver you? Behold, My rebuke dries up the sea; I turn the rivers into a desert; the fish rot for lack of water and die of thirst. (50:2).
I clothe the heavens in black and make sackcloth their covering.” (50:3).
The Lord GOD has given Me the tongue of discipleship, to sustain the weary with a word. He awakens Me morning by morning; He awakens My ear to listen as a disciple. (50:4).
The Lord GOD has opened My ears, and I have not been rebellious, nor have I turned back. (50:5).
I offered My back to those who struck Me, and My cheeks to those who tore out My beard. I did not hide My face from scorn and spittle. (50:6).
Because the Lord GOD helps Me, I have not been disgraced; therefore I have set My face like flint, and I know that I will not be put to shame. (50:7).
The One who vindicates Me is near. Who will dare to contend with Me? Let us confront each other! Who has a case against Me? Let him approach Me! (50:8).
Surely the Lord GOD helps Me. Who is there to condemn Me? See, they will all wear out like a garment; the moths will devour them. (50:9).
Who among you fears the LORD and obeys the voice of His Servant? Who among you walks in darkness and has no light? Let him trust in the name of the LORD; let him lean on his God. (50:10).

Behold, all you who kindle a fire, who array yourselves with firebrands, walk in the light of your fire and of the firebrands you have lit! This is what you will receive from My hand: You will lie down in a place of torment. (50:11).
crossRefs: Deuteronomy 24:1-4: The law of the certificate of divorce, the document Isaiah 50:1 demands be produced.
Matthew 26:67: At the trial they spit in Jesus' face and struck Him, and others slapped Him.
1 Peter 2:23: When they heaped abuse on Him He did not retaliate, but entrusted Himself to the One who judges justly.
Luke 9:51: As the day of His ascension approached, Jesus resolutely set out for Jerusalem.
Ezekiel 3:8-9: The LORD makes the prophet's forehead like a diamond, harder than flint, so he will not fear a rebellious house.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: שַׂמְתִּי פָנַי כַּחַּלָּמִישׁ, Greek (LXX): ἔθηκα τὸ πρόσωπόν μου ὡς στερεὸν, Aramaic: קַבַּעְתִּי אַפַּי כְּצֻר
translationNotes.note: Fixed resolve amid abuse (50:7).

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: שַׂק (saq); Greek: σάκκος (sakkos)
translationNotes.note: A coarse, dark goat-hair fabric worn against bare skin as a universal sign of mourning, repentance, or distress (1 Kings 21:27; Jonah 3:5; Matthew 11:21). Wearing it publicly broadcast grief or contrition; the discomfort itself was part of the symbolism.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: סֵפֶר כְּרִיתוּת (sepher kerithuth, a document of cutting off)
translationNotes.note: 50:1 names two legal instruments and asks to see the paperwork for either. A husband who divorced his wife had to put it in writing and hand it to her, which is the requirement at Deuteronomy 24:1-3, and the document was her protection. A man in debt could sell his children into service to clear it, which 2 Kings 4:1 and Nehemiah 5:5 show happening. The verse asks where the writ is and which creditor was paid, and answers that there was neither.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: לְמֹרְטִים (le-morettim, to those who pluck out)
translationNotes.note: The three things listed at 50:6 are not random violence, they are calculated humiliations. Beards were a mark of standing, so pulling one out was a public unmaking; when Hanun shaved off half the beards of David's envoys at 2 Samuel 10:4-5 it was an act of war and the men were kept away until they grew back. Spitting in the face carried disgrace in law as well, at Numbers 12:14 and Deuteronomy 25:9.

translationNotes.term: Morning by morning he awakens my ear
translationNotes.original: Hebrew: לְשׁוֹן לִמּוּדִים (leshon limmudim, the tongue of the taught)
translationNotes.note: 50:4 uses the vocabulary of a pupil, not a master. Limmudim are those under instruction, the same word for disciples at 8:16. The verse has the ear woken each morning to listen like one being taught, and the purpose given is to know how to sustain with a word the one who is weary. 50:5 then says the ear was opened and he was not rebellious.

stories.keyTakeaway: God denies divorcing Israel or selling them into bondage, asserting his power to rescue; a servant describes receiving instruction from God, enduring beatings and mockery, and trusting God's vindication. Those who fear the LORD should trust him in darkness, while those who rely on their own fires will lie down in torment.

stories.title: 🛤️ Isaiah 51
summaryBullets: “Listen to Me, you who pursue righteousness, you who seek the LORD: Look to the rock from which you were cut, and to the quarry from which you were hewn. (51:1).
Look to Abraham your father, and to Sarah who gave you birth. When I called him, he was but one; then I blessed him and multiplied him. (51:2).

For the LORD will comfort Zion and will look with compassion on all her ruins; He will make her wilderness like Eden and her desert like the garden of the LORD. Joy and gladness will be found in her, thanksgiving and melodious song. (51:3).
Pay attention to Me, My people, and listen to Me, My nation; for a law will go out from Me, and My justice will become a light to the nations; I will bring it about quickly. (51:4).
My righteousness draws near, My salvation is on the way, and My arms will bring justice to the nations. The islands will look for Me and wait in hope for My arm. (51:5).

Lift up your eyes to the heavens, and look at the earth below; for the heavens will vanish like smoke, the earth will wear out like a garment, and its people will die like gnats. But My salvation will last forever, and My righteousness will never fail. (51:6).
Listen to Me, you who know what is right, you people with My law in your hearts: Do not fear the scorn of men; do not be broken by their insults. (51:7).
For the moth will devour them like a garment, and the worm will eat them like wool. But My righteousness will last forever, My salvation through all generations.” (51:8).
Awake, awake, put on strength, O arm of the LORD. Wake up as in days past, as in generations of old. Was it not You who cut Rahab to pieces, who pierced through the dragon? (51:9).
Was it not You who dried up the sea, the waters of the great deep, who made a road in the depths of the sea for the redeemed to cross over? (51:10).
So the redeemed of the LORD will return and enter Zion with singing, crowned with everlasting joy. Gladness and joy will overtake them, and sorrow and sighing will flee. (51:11).
“I, even I, am He who comforts you. Why should you be afraid of mortal man, of a son of man who withers like grass? (51:12).

But you have forgotten the LORD, your Maker, who stretched out the heavens and laid the foundations of the earth. You live in terror all day long because of the fury of the oppressor who is bent on destruction. But where is the fury of the oppressor? (51:13).
The captive will soon be freed; he will not die in the dungeon, and his bread will not be lacking. (51:14).
For I am the LORD your God who stirs up the sea so that its waves roar— the LORD of Hosts is His name. (51:15).
I have put My words in your mouth, and covered you with the shadow of My hand, to establish the heavens, to found the earth, and to say to Zion, ‘You are My people.’” (51:16).
Awake, awake! Rise up, O Jerusalem, you who have drunk from the hand of the LORD the cup of His fury; you who have drained the goblet to the dregs — the cup that makes men stagger. (51:17).
Among all the sons she bore, there is no one to guide her; among all the sons she brought up, there is no one to take her hand. (51:18).
These pairs have befallen you: devastation and destruction, famine and sword. Who will grieve for you? Who can comfort you? (51:19).
Your sons have fainted; they lie at the head of every street, like an antelope in a net. They are full of the wrath of the LORD, the rebuke of your God. (51:20).
Therefore now hear this, you afflicted one, drunken, but not with wine. (51:21).

Thus says your Lord, the LORD, even your God, who defends His people: “See, I have removed from your hand the cup of staggering. From that goblet, the cup of My fury, you will never drink again. (51:22).
I will place it in the hands of your tormentors, who told you: ‘Lie down, so we can walk over you,’ so that you made your back like the ground, like a street to be traversed.” (51:23).
crossRefs: Genesis 12:1-3: The LORD calls Abram out of his country alone and promises to make him into a great nation.
Genesis 18:11-14: Sarah is past childbearing and laughs, and the LORD asks whether anything is too difficult for Him.
Psalm 89:10: 'You crushed Rahab like a carcass; You scattered Your enemies with Your mighty arm.'
Exodus 14:21-22: The LORD drives back the sea with a strong east wind and the Israelites go through on dry ground.
Jeremiah 25:15-17: The cup of the wine of wrath is put in the prophet's hand and the nations are made to drink it and stagger.

translationNotes.term: The quarry from which you were hewn
translationNotes.original: Hebrew: מַקֶּבֶת בּוֹר (maqqevet bor)
translationNotes.note: Building stone was cut out of a rock face by scoring a channel around the block with picks, undercutting it, and levering it free, leaving a pit with squared scars. Verse 2 names the quarry: Abraham and Sarah, one man and one barren woman, from whom the whole nation was cut.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: רַהַב (Rahab) - Hebrew: תַּנִּין (tannin)
translationNotes.note: This Rahab is not the woman of Jericho; the spelling is different and Scripture uses this name for Egypt (Psalm 87:4; Isaiah 30:7, where Egypt is called Rahab who sits still). Tannin is a sea monster or serpent. Verse 10 states what verse 9 means by it: the drying of the sea and the road made through the deep for the redeemed to cross, which is Exodus 14:21-22.

translationNotes.term: The cup that makes men stagger
translationNotes.original: Hebrew: כּוֹס הַתַּרְעֵלָה (kos ha-tarelah)
translationNotes.note: The image comes from the table, where the host pours and the guest must drink what he is handed. Scripture uses the cup for a portion measured out by God: Psalm 75:8 has it foaming and mixed, Jeremiah 25:15-17 has the prophet carrying it around to the nations, and Habakkuk 2:16 turns it back on the one who poured. Verse 22 takes it out of Jerusalem's hand and puts it into her tormentors'.

translationNotes.term: Like an antelope in a net
translationNotes.original: Hebrew: תוֹא מִכְמָר (to mikhmar)
translationNotes.note: Hunters drove wild game toward nets strung across a gap or a ravine; the animal hit the mesh, tangled, and thrashed itself out. The to is a wild ox or antelope, listed among the clean wild game a man could eat in Deuteronomy 14:5. Verse 20 has the sons of the city lying at every street corner like that.

translationNotes.term: Lie down, so we can walk over you
translationNotes.original: Hebrew: שְׁחִי וְנַעֲבֹרָה (shechi ve-naavorah)
translationNotes.note: Treading on a defeated man was a formal act of conquest, not casual cruelty. Joshua 10:24 has the commanders of Israel put their feet on the necks of the five captured kings before they are executed, and Egyptian and Assyrian palace art shows the king standing on his enemies. Verse 23 has Jerusalem made into a road surface.

stories.keyTakeaway: God calls Israel to remember Abraham and promises to comfort Zion with restoration and righteousness that will endure forever, while instructing the afflicted not to fear their oppressors since he will rescue prisoners and transfer the cup of his wrath from them to their tormentors.

stories.title: 🛤️ Isaiah 52
summaryBullets: Awake, awake, clothe yourself with strength, O Zion! Put on your garments of splendor, O Jerusalem, holy city! For the uncircumcised and unclean will no longer enter you. (52:1).
Shake off your dust! Rise up and sit on your throne, O Jerusalem. Remove the chains from your neck, O captive Daughter of Zion. (52:2).
For this is what the LORD says: “You were sold for nothing, and without money you will be redeemed.” (52:3).
For this is what the Lord GOD says: “At first My people went down to Egypt to live, then Assyria oppressed them without cause. (52:4).
And now what have I here? declares the LORD. For My people have been taken without cause; those who rule them taunt, declares the LORD, and My name is blasphemed continually all day long. (52:5).
Therefore My people will know My name; therefore they will know on that day that I am He who speaks. Here I am!” (52:6).
How beautiful on the mountains are the feet of those who bring good news, who proclaim peace, who bring good tidings, who proclaim salvation, who say to Zion, “Your God reigns!” (52:7).
Listen! Your watchmen lift up their voices, together they shout for joy. For every eye will see when the LORD returns to Zion. (52:8).
Break forth in joy, sing together, O ruins of Jerusalem, for the LORD has comforted His people; He has redeemed Jerusalem. (52:9).
The LORD has bared His holy arm in the sight of all the nations; all the ends of the earth will see the salvation of our God. (52:10).
Depart, depart, go out from there! Touch no unclean thing; come out from it, purify yourselves, you who carry the vessels of the LORD. (52:11).
For you will not leave in a hurry nor flee in haste, for the LORD goes before you, and the God of Israel is your rear guard. (52:12).
Behold, My Servant will prosper; He will be raised and lifted up and highly exalted. (52:13).
Just as many were appalled at Him— His appearance was disfigured beyond that of any man, and His form was marred beyond human likeness— (52:14).
so He will sprinkle many nations. Kings will shut their mouths because of Him. For they will see what they have not been told, and they will understand what they have not heard. (52:15).
crossRefs: Romans 10:15: Paul quotes Isaiah 52:7, 'How beautiful are the feet of those who bring good news!'
Nahum 1:15: 'Look to the mountains, the feet of one who brings good news, who proclaims peace,' and Judah is told to keep her feasts.
Romans 15:21: Paul quotes Isaiah 52:15 to explain his mission: those who were not told about Him will see, and those who have not heard will understand.
2 Corinthians 6:17: 'Come out from among them and be separate, says the Lord. Touch no unclean thing, and I will receive you.'
Exodus 12:11: Israel eats the first Passover in haste, dressed for travel with sandals on and staff in hand, the opposite of the departure promised here.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: כּוֹס חֵמָה (kos ḥemah), Greek (LXX): ποτήριον θυμοῦ, Aramaic: כס דְּרוּגְזָא
translationNotes.note: Image of forced suffering, later transferred to oppressors (51:17-23).

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: מְבַשֵּׂר שָׁלוֹם (mevaser shalom), Greek (LXX): εὐαγγελιζόμενος εἰρήνην, Aramaic: מבשר שלמא
translationNotes.note: Herald announces God’s kingship (52:7).

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: הִבָּרוּ… צְאוּ (hibbaru… tseʾu), Greek (LXX): ἁγνίσθητε… ἐξέρχεσθε, Aramaic: אִתְדַּכּוּ… פְּקוּ
translationNotes.note: Ritual/moral separation in leaving Babylon (52:11).

stories.keyTakeaway: Jerusalem is called to awake and shed its captivity, assured that God will redeem his people at no cost and restore them; a servant will arise, disfigured yet exalted, who will bring salvation to the nations and silence kings.

stories.title: ✝️ Isaiah 53
summaryBullets: Who has believed our message? And to whom has the arm of the LORD been revealed? (53:1).
He grew up before Him like a tender shoot, and like a root out of dry ground. He had no stately form or majesty to attract us, no beauty that we should desire Him. (53:2).
He was despised and rejected by men, a man of sorrows, acquainted with grief. Like one from whom men hide their faces, He was despised, and we esteemed Him not. (53:3).
Surely He took up our infirmities and carried our sorrows; yet we considered Him stricken, struck down by God, and afflicted. (53:4).
But He was pierced for our transgressions, He was crushed for our iniquities; the punishment that brought us peace was upon Him, and by His stripes we are healed. (53:5).
We all like sheep have gone astray, each one has turned to his own way; and the LORD has laid upon Him the iniquity of us all. (53:6).
He was oppressed and afflicted, yet He did not open His mouth. He was led like a lamb to the slaughter, and as a sheep before her shearers is silent, so He did not open His mouth. (53:7).
By oppression and judgment He was taken away, and who can recount His descendants? For He was cut off from the land of the living; He was stricken for the transgression of My people. (53:8).
He was assigned a grave with the wicked, and with a rich man in His death, although He had done no violence, nor was any deceit in His mouth. (53:9).

Yet it was the LORD’s will to crush Him and to cause Him to suffer; and when His soul is made a guilt offering, He will see His offspring, He will prolong His days, and the good pleasure of the LORD will prosper in His hand. (53:10).
After the anguish of His soul, He will see the light of life and be satisfied. By His knowledge My righteous Servant will justify many, and He will bear their iniquities. (53:11).

Therefore I will allot Him a portion with the great, and He will divide the spoils with the strong, because He has poured out His life unto death, and He was numbered with the transgressors. Yet He bore the sin of many and made intercession for the transgressors. (53:12).
crossRefs: Acts 8:32-35: Isaiah 53 read and explained.
1 Peter 2:22-25: “He committed no sin… by his wounds you were healed.”
Mark 15:28: “Numbered with transgressors.”

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: אָשָׁם (ʾasham), Greek (LXX): περὶ ἁμαρτίας / πλημμέλειας, Aramaic: אָשָׁם
translationNotes.note: Sacrificial term; his life is presented as an offering (53:10).

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: מְחֹלָל / מְדֻכָּא (meḥolal / medukkaʾ), Greek (LXX): τετρώμενος / μεμαλακισμένος, Aramaic: מדקר / מדכא
translationNotes.note: Violent harm terms describing his suffering (53:5).

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: יַצְדִּיק צַדִּיק עֲבְדִּי לָרַבִּים, Greek (LXX): δικαιῶσαι δίκαιον εὖ δουλεύσαντα πολλοῖς, Aramaic: יְזַכֵּא צַדִּיק עַבְדִּי לְסַגִּיאִין
translationNotes.note: Legal declaration imagery (53:11).

stories.keyTakeaway: The Servant suffers innocently, bears the guilt of many, dies, and yet is promised life and success.

stories.title: 🌧️ Isaiah 54
summaryBullets: “Shout for joy, O barren woman, who bears no children; break forth in song and cry aloud, you who have never travailed; because more are the children of the desolate woman than of her who has a husband,” says the LORD. (54:1).
“Enlarge the site of your tent, stretch out the curtains of your dwellings, do not hold back. Lengthen your ropes and drive your stakes in deep. (54:2).
For you will spread out to the right and left; your descendants will dispossess the nations and inhabit the desolate cities. (54:3).

Do not be afraid, for you will not be put to shame; do not be intimidated, for you will not be humiliated. For you will forget the shame of your youth and will remember no more the reproach of your widowhood. (54:4).
For your husband is your Maker — the LORD of Hosts is His name— the Holy One of Israel is your Redeemer; He is called the God of all the earth. (54:5).
For the LORD has called you back, like a wife deserted and wounded in spirit, like the rejected wife of one’s youth,” says your God. (54:6).
“For a brief moment I forsook you, but with great compassion I will bring you back. (54:7).
In a surge of anger I hid My face from you for a moment, but with everlasting kindness I will have compassion on you,” says the LORD your Redeemer. (54:8).
“For to Me this is like the days of Noah, when I swore that the waters of Noah would never again cover the earth. So I have sworn that I will not be angry with you or rebuke you. (54:9).

Though the mountains may be removed and the hills may be shaken, My loving devotion will not depart from you, and My covenant of peace will not be broken,” says the LORD, who has compassion on you. (54:10).
“O afflicted city, lashed by storms, without solace, surely I will set your stones in antimony and lay your foundations with sapphires. (54:11).
I will make your pinnacles of rubies, your gates of sparkling jewels, and all your walls of precious stones. (54:12).
Then all your sons will be taught by the LORD, and great will be their prosperity. (54:13).
In righteousness you will be established, far from oppression, for you will have no fear. Terror will be far removed, for it will not come near you. (54:14).
If anyone attacks you, it is not from Me; whoever assails you will fall before you. (54:15).
Behold, I have created the craftsman who fans the coals into flame and forges a weapon fit for its task; and I have created the destroyer to wreak havoc. (54:16).

No weapon formed against you shall prosper, and you will refute every tongue that accuses you. This is the heritage of the servants of the LORD, and their vindication is from Me,” declares the LORD. (54:17).
crossRefs: Galatians 4:27: Paul quotes Isaiah 54:1, 'Rejoice, O barren woman, who bears no children,' and applies it to the Jerusalem above.
Genesis 9:11-15: After the flood God swears that the waters will never again destroy all life and sets the rainbow in the clouds as the sign.
Jeremiah 31:35-37: The fixed order of sun, moon, and roaring sea is given as the pledge that Israel will never cease to be a nation.
Revelation 21:18-21: The city's foundations are adorned with every kind of precious stone and its twelve gates are twelve pearls.
Isaiah 49:20-21: The children of the bereaved crowd her and say the place is too small, and she asks who bore them for her.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: עֲקָרָה (aqarah)
translationNotes.note: Childlessness was a public reproach and a practical catastrophe, since children were a woman's standing in the household and her only support in old age. Sarah, Rebekah, Rachel, Hannah, and the Shunammite woman all live under it (Genesis 16:1; 25:21; 30:1; 1 Samuel 1:6-8; 2 Kings 4:14). Paul quotes this verse word for word in Galatians 4:27.

translationNotes.term: Lengthen your ropes and drive your stakes
translationNotes.original: Hebrew: יְתֵדֹתַיִךְ (yetedotayikh)
translationNotes.note: A tent of woven black goat hair is enlarged by adding panels of cloth, which means longer guy ropes and pegs driven further out and deeper to hold the extra pull. Every listener had done it. Jeremiah 10:20 uses the same picture in reverse, a tent destroyed with the cords snapped and no one left to pitch it.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: מֵי נֹחַ (mey Noach)
translationNotes.note: The appeal is to a specific sworn undertaking. Genesis 8:21-22 and 9:11-17 record God swearing never again to cut off all flesh by a flood and setting the bow in the cloud as the standing sign of it. Verse 9 says the promise being made here has the same sworn character.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: פּוּךְ (pukh) - Hebrew: סַפִּיר (sappir)
translationNotes.note: Pukh is the black mineral eye paint of the ancient world, ground and lined around the eye to make it stand out; Jezebel put pukh on her eyes in 2 Kings 9:30 and Jeremiah 4:30 names it as a woman's paint. Here it is the dark bed the building stones are set in, so the wall is made up like an eye. Sappir in the Old Testament is lapis lazuli, the deep blue stone under God's feet in Exodus 24:10; blue corundum, the modern sapphire, was not being cut in this period.

translationNotes.term: The craftsman who fans the coals
translationNotes.original: Hebrew: חָרָשׁ (charash)
translationNotes.note: A smith worked a charcoal hearth with skin bellows, drew out a bloom of hot iron, and hammered it into shape on a stone or an anvil, quenching and reworking it. The trade was strategic: 1 Samuel 13:19-22 records that no smith was to be found in Israel because the Philistines allowed none, so Israelites had to go down to them even to sharpen a plow point, and on the day of battle only Saul and Jonathan had a sword.

stories.keyTakeaway: The LORD calls the barren woman to rejoice because her descendants will multiply and reclaim desolate cities; he promises to rebuild her with precious stones, teach her children in righteousness, and protect her from weapons and accusers with everlasting kindness.

stories.title: 🌧️ Isaiah 55
summaryBullets: “Come, all you who are thirsty, come to the waters; and you without money, come, buy, and eat! Come, buy wine and milk without money and without cost! (55:1).
Why spend money on that which is not bread, and your labor on that which does not satisfy? Listen carefully to Me, and eat what is good, and your soul will delight in the richest of foods. (55:2).
Incline your ear and come to Me; listen, so that your soul may live. I will make with you an everlasting covenant — My loving devotion promised to David. (55:3).
Behold, I have made him a witness to the nations, a leader and commander of the peoples. (55:4).
Surely you will summon a nation you do not know, and nations who do not know you will run to you. For the LORD your God, the Holy One of Israel, has bestowed glory on you.” (55:5).
Seek the LORD while He may be found; call on Him while He is near. (55:6).
Let the wicked man forsake his way and the unrighteous man his thoughts; let him return to the LORD, that He may have compassion, and to our God, for He will freely pardon. (55:7).
“For My thoughts are not your thoughts, neither are your ways My ways,” declares the LORD. (55:8).
“For as the heavens are higher than the earth, so My ways are higher than your ways and My thoughts than your thoughts. (55:9).
For just as rain and snow fall from heaven and do not return without watering the earth, making it bud and sprout, and providing seed to sow and food to eat, (55:10).
so My word that proceeds from My mouth will not return to Me empty, but it will accomplish what I please, and it will prosper where I send it. (55:11).
You will indeed go out with joy and be led forth in peace; the mountains and hills will burst into song before you, and all the trees of the field will clap their hands. (55:12).
Instead of the thornbush, the cypress will grow, and instead of the brier, the myrtle will spring up; this will make a name for the LORD, an everlasting sign, never to be destroyed.” (55:13).
crossRefs: John 7:37-38: Jesus stands at the feast and calls out that anyone who is thirsty should come to Him and drink.
Revelation 22:17: The Spirit and the bride say 'Come,' and the one who is thirsty may take the water of life freely.
Acts 13:34: Paul cites the promise of Isaiah 55:3 as fulfilled in the resurrection: 'I will give you the holy and sure blessings promised to David.'
2 Samuel 7:12-16: The LORD promises David a descendant whose throne He will establish forever, the covenant behind the sure mercies named here.
Deuteronomy 32:1-2: Moses asks that his teaching fall like rain and settle like dew, the same picture of a word that waters the ground.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: בְּרִית שָׁלוֹם (berit shalom), Greek (LXX): διαθήκη εἰρήνης, Aramaic: קְיָם דִּשְׁלָם
translationNotes.note: Assurance of lasting protection (54:10).

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: בְּלוֹא כֶסֶף… בְּלוֹא מְחִיר, Greek (LXX): ἄνευ ἀργυρίου… ἄνευ τιμῆς, Aramaic: בְּלָא כספא… בְּלָא דָמִים
translationNotes.note: Offer of free provision (55:1).

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: לֹא יָשׁוּב רֵיקָם, Greek (LXX): οὐ μὴ ἐπιστρέψῃ κενόν, Aramaic: לָא יְתוּב רֵיקָם
translationNotes.note: Guarantee of God’s effective speech (55:11).

stories.keyTakeaway: Isaiah invites the thirsty and poor to receive sustenance freely and calls the wicked to turn to the Lord for mercy; God declares his thoughts and ways surpass human understanding, and his word accomplishes its purpose like rain watering the earth.

stories.title: 🌍 Isaiah 56
summaryBullets: This is what the LORD says: “Maintain justice and do what is right, for My salvation is coming soon, and My righteousness will be revealed. (56:1).
Blessed is the man who does this, and the son of man who holds it fast, who keeps the Sabbath without profaning it and keeps his hand from doing any evil.” (56:2).
Let no foreigner who has joined himself to the LORD say, “The LORD will utterly exclude me from His people.” And let the eunuch not say, “I am but a dry tree.” (56:3).
For this is what the LORD says: “To the eunuchs who keep My Sabbaths, who choose what pleases Me and hold fast to My covenant — (56:4).
I will give them, in My house and within My walls, a memorial and a name better than that of sons and daughters. I will give them an everlasting name that will not be cut off. (56:5).

And the foreigners who join themselves to the LORD to minister to Him, to love the name of the LORD, and to be His servants — all who keep the Sabbath without profaning it and who hold fast to My covenant— (56:6).

I will bring them to My holy mountain and make them joyful in My house of prayer. Their burnt offerings and sacrifices will be accepted on My altar, for My house will be called a house of prayer for all the nations.” (56:7).
Thus declares the Lord GOD, who gathers the dispersed of Israel: “I will gather to them still others besides those already gathered.” (56:8).
Come, all you beasts of the field; eat greedily, all you beasts of the forest. (56:9).
Israel’s watchmen are blind, they are all oblivious; they are all mute dogs, they cannot bark; they are dreamers lying around, loving to slumber. (56:10).
Like ravenous dogs, they are never satisfied. They are shepherds with no discernment; they all turn to their own way, each one seeking his own gain: (56:11).
“Come, let me get the wine, let us imbibe the strong drink, and tomorrow will be like today, only far better!” (56:12).
crossRefs: Deuteronomy 23:1-8: The law barring the emasculated man and certain foreigners from the assembly of the LORD.
Acts 8:26-39: An Ethiopian court official, a eunuch, is reading Isaiah on the desert road to Gaza when Philip explains it and baptizes him.
Mark 11:17: Jesus clears the temple, quoting 'My house will be called a house of prayer for all the nations.'
1 Kings 8:41-43: Solomon prays that the LORD hear the foreigner who comes from a distant land because of His name and prays toward the temple.
Ezekiel 34:1-10: Woe is pronounced on the shepherds of Israel who feed themselves, eat the fat, and do not feed the flock.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: סָרִיס (saris), Greek (LXX): εὐνοῦχος, Aramaic: מְהֵימַן/סריס
translationNotes.note: Previously excluded (Deut 23:1), now welcomed when keeping covenant (56:3-5).

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: בֵּית תְּפִלָּה, Greek (LXX): οἶκος προσευχῆς, Aramaic: בֵּית צְלוֹתָא
translationNotes.note: Temple’s global role (56:7).

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: שַׁבָּת (shabbat); Greek: σάββατον (sabbaton)
translationNotes.note: The seventh day, set apart by God's command (Exodus 20:8-11). All work ceased from sunset Friday to sunset Saturday. By Jesus' day, rabbinical tradition had elaborated 39 categories of forbidden labor; many of Jesus' healings deliberately challenged those additional rules without violating the Torah command itself.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: יָד וָשֵׁם (yad va-shem)
translationNotes.note: 56:5 promises the childless a yad and a shem inside the temple, better than sons and daughters. A yad is literally a hand and also a standing monument stone: 2 Samuel 18:18 has Absalom set one up in his lifetime, saying he had no son to keep his name alive, and the text notes it was called Absalom's monument. So the promise is exactly the thing a man without children erected for himself, given by God instead.

translationNotes.term: The foreigner joined to the LORD
translationNotes.original: Hebrew: בֶּן־הַנֵּכָר (ben ha-nekhar, son of the foreigner)
translationNotes.note: 56:3 and 56:6 name a second excluded class beside the eunuch. The assembly was closed to certain foreigners by descent under Deuteronomy 23:3, and a ben nekhar was outside the covenant by definition. What 56:6-7 attaches the promise to is not ancestry but three things a man does: holding the sabbath, holding the covenant, and serving. 56:8 then says more will be gathered besides those already gathered.

stories.keyTakeaway: The LORD calls Israel to maintain justice and keep the Sabbath, promising to include foreigners and eunuchs in his covenant if they obey; he then condemns Israel's blind watchmen and corrupt shepherds who pursue their own gain instead of guarding the people.

stories.title: 🌍 Isaiah 57
summaryBullets: The righteous perish, and no one takes it to heart; devout men are taken away, while no one considers that the righteous are taken away from the presence of evil. (57:1).
Those who walk uprightly enter into peace; they find rest, lying down in death. (57:2).
“But come here, you sons of a sorceress, you offspring of adulterers and prostitutes! (57:3).
Whom are you mocking? At whom do you sneer and stick out your tongue? Are you not children of transgression, offspring of deceit, (57:4).
who burn with lust among the oaks, under every luxuriant tree, who slaughter your children in the valleys, under the clefts of the rocks? (57:5).

Your portion is among the smooth stones of the valley; indeed, they are your lot. Even to them you have poured out a drink offering and offered a grain offering. Should I relent because of these? (57:6).
On a high and lofty hill you have made your bed, and there you went up to offer sacrifices. (57:7).

Behind the door and doorpost you have set up your memorial. Forsaking Me, you uncovered your bed; you climbed up and opened it wide. And you have made a pact with those whose bed you have loved; you have gazed upon their nakedness. (57:8).
You went to Molech with oil and multiplied your perfumes. You have sent your envoys a great distance; you have descended even to Sheol itself. (57:9).
You are wearied by your many journeys, but you did not say, “There is no hope!” You found renewal of your strength; therefore you did not grow weak. (57:10).
Whom have you dreaded and feared, so that you lied and failed to remember Me or take this to heart? Is it not because I have long been silent that you do not fear Me? (57:11).
I will expose your righteousness and your works, and they will not profit you. (57:12).

When you cry out, let your companies of idols deliver you! Yet the wind will carry off all of them, a breath will take them away. But he who seeks refuge in Me will inherit the land and possess My holy mountain.” (57:13).
And it will be said, “Build it up, build it up, prepare the way, take every obstacle out of the way of My people.” (57:14).

For thus says the One who is high and lifted up, who inhabits eternity, whose name is Holy: “I dwell in a high and holy place, and with the oppressed and humble in spirit, to restore the spirit of the lowly and revive the heart of the contrite. (57:15).
For I will not accuse you forever, nor will I always be angry; for then the spirit of man would grow weak before Me— the breath of life I have made. (57:16).
I was enraged by his sinful greed, so I struck him and hid My face in anger; yet he kept turning back to the desires of his heart. (57:17).
I have seen his ways, but I will heal him; I will guide him and restore comfort to him and his mourners, (57:18).
bringing praise to their lips. Peace, peace to those far and near,” says the LORD, “and I will heal them.” (57:19).
But the wicked are like the storm-tossed sea, for it cannot be still, and its waves churn up mire and muck. (57:20).
“There is no peace,” says my God, “for the wicked.” (57:21).
crossRefs: 2 Kings 23:10: Josiah desecrates Topheth in the Valley of Ben-hinnom so that no one can sacrifice a son or daughter in the fire to Molech.
Leviticus 18:21: 'You must not give any of your children to be sacrificed to Molech, for you must not profane the name of your God.'
Ephesians 2:17: 'He came and preached peace to you who were far away and peace to those who were near,' the pairing of Isaiah 57:19.
Psalm 34:18: 'The LORD is near to the brokenhearted; He saves the contrite in spirit.'
Isaiah 48:22: The same refrain closed the previous section: 'There is no peace,' says the LORD, 'for the wicked.'

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: דַּכָּא / שְׁפַל־רוּחַ, Greek (LXX): ταπεινός / ταπεινὸς τῷ πνεύματι, Aramaic: דַּכָּא / מִכְתַּת רוּחָא
translationNotes.note: Inner posture God revives (57:15).

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: שְׁאוֹל (sheol)
translationNotes.note: The Old Testament realm of the dead; a shadowy underworld where both righteous and wicked descend (Genesis 37:35; Psalm 16:10). Not necessarily a place of torment; more a state of cessation and silence. The Septuagint and New Testament render it with the Greek word hades.

translationNotes.term: The smooth stones of the valley
translationNotes.original: Hebrew: בְּחַלְּקֵי־נַחַל חֶלְקֵךְ (be-chalqe nachal chelqekh)
translationNotes.note: 57:6 is a pun that English has to throw away: chalqe, the smooth ones of the wadi, and chelqekh, your portion, from the same sound. A nachal is a dry streambed that runs only after rain, and its floor is worn stones. The verse says the water-polished stones down in the gully are all the inheritance you get, and that drink offerings and grain offerings were poured out to them.

translationNotes.term: Slaughtering the children in the valleys
translationNotes.original: Hebrew: שֹׁחֲטֵי הַיְלָדִים בַּנְּחָלִים (shochate ha-yeladim ba-nechalim)
translationNotes.note: 57:5 states plainly what was being done under the oaks and in the clefts of the rocks: children killed as offerings. The site outside Jerusalem where it happened was the Topheth in the Valley of Ben Hinnom, named at 30:33 and at Jeremiah 7:31 and 32:35, and 2 Kings 23:10 has Josiah destroy it to stop the practice. The Greek name of that valley is Gehenna, the word Jesus uses for hell.

translationNotes.term: You journeyed to the king with oil
translationNotes.original: Hebrew: וַתָּשֻׁרִי לַמֶּלֶךְ בַּשֶּׁמֶן (va-tashuri la-melekh ba-shamen)
translationNotes.note: The word at 57:9 is melekh, the king, and the same consonants stand behind the name Molech, so versions divide between the king and the god. Either way the verse describes a diplomatic errand run like a courtship: perfumed oil, piled-up scents, envoys sent far off, and 57:9 ends with sending down as far as Sheol.

translationNotes.term: Your bed on a high mountain
translationNotes.original: Hebrew: בָּמָה (bamah, high place)
translationNotes.note: The bamah was a raised open-air shrine, usually on a hilltop, with an altar and often a standing stone and a wooden pole. 57:7 puts the bed on one and 57:8 puts the memorial behind the door, which is where the law told Israel to write the commandments (Deuteronomy 6:9). Both halves of the picture take something the covenant assigned and hand it to someone else.

stories.keyTakeaway: God condemns the people's idolatry, false worship, and unfaithfulness while offering to heal and comfort the contrite; the wicked, however, will find no peace.

headings.text: The Blessed Death of the Righteous

stories.title: 🕯️ Isaiah 58
summaryBullets: “Cry aloud, do not hold back! Raise your voice like a ram’s horn. Declare to My people their transgression and to the house of Jacob their sins. (58:1).

For day after day they seek Me and delight to know My ways, like a nation that does what is right and does not forsake the justice of their God. They ask Me for righteous judgments; they delight in the nearness of God.” (58:2).
“Why have we fasted, and You have not seen? Why have we humbled ourselves, and You have not noticed?” “Behold, on the day of your fast, you do as you please, and you oppress all your workers. (58:3).
You fast with contention and strife to strike viciously with your fist. You cannot fast as you do today and have your voice be heard on high. (58:4).

Is this the fast I have chosen: a day for a man to deny himself, to bow his head like a reed, and to spread out sackcloth and ashes? Will you call this a fast and a day acceptable to the LORD? (58:5).
Isn’t this the fast that I have chosen: to break the chains of wickedness, to untie the cords of the yoke, to set the oppressed free and tear off every yoke? (58:6).
Isn’t it to share your bread with the hungry, to bring the poor and homeless into your home, to clothe the naked when you see him, and not to turn away from your own flesh and blood? (58:7).
Then your light will break forth like the dawn, and your healing will come quickly. Your righteousness will go before you, and the glory of the LORD will be your rear guard. (58:8).
Then you will call, and the LORD will answer; you will cry out, and He will say, ‘Here I am.’ If you remove the yoke from your midst, the pointing of the finger and malicious talk, (58:9).
and if you give yourself to the hungry and satisfy the afflicted soul, then your light will go forth in the darkness, and your night will be like noonday. (58:10).
The LORD will always guide you; He will satisfy you in a sun-scorched land and strengthen your frame. You will be like a well-watered garden, like a spring whose waters never fail. (58:11).
Your people will rebuild the ancient ruins; you will restore the age-old foundations; you will be called Repairer of the Breach, Restorer of the Streets of Dwelling. (58:12).

If you turn your foot from breaking the Sabbath, from doing as you please on My holy day, if you call the Sabbath a delight, and the LORD’s holy day honorable, if you honor it by not going your own way or seeking your own pleasure or speaking idle words, (58:13).
then you will delight yourself in the LORD, and I will make you ride on the heights of the land and feed you with the heritage of your father Jacob.” For the mouth of the LORD has spoken. (58:14).
crossRefs: Leviticus 16:29-31: The one fast the law commands, on the tenth day of the seventh month, when Israel humbles itself and does no work.
Zechariah 7:4-6: The LORD asks whether seventy years of fasting in the fifth and seventh months were really for Him or for themselves.
Matthew 6:16-18: Fast without a somber face, so the fasting is seen by the Father who is unseen rather than by men.
Deuteronomy 15:7-11: Israel is commanded not to harden the heart or shut the hand against a poor brother, but to open the hand wide.
Nehemiah 13:15-16: Nehemiah finds Judeans treading winepresses on the Sabbath and men of Tyre selling fish and merchandise in Jerusalem.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: הֲלוֹא זֶה צוֹם אֶבְחָרֵהוּ, Greek (LXX): οὐχὶ τοιοῦτος νηστεία ἐγὼ ἐξελεξάμην, Aramaic: הָא צֹום דְּבְחַרְתֵּיהּ
translationNotes.note: Defines true fasting as justice and mercy (58:6-7).

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: שַׂק (saq); Greek: σάκκος (sakkos)
translationNotes.note: A coarse, dark goat-hair fabric worn against bare skin as a universal sign of mourning, repentance, or distress (1 Kings 21:27; Jonah 3:5; Matthew 11:21). Wearing it publicly broadcast grief or contrition; the discomfort itself was part of the symbolism.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: שַׁבָּת (shabbat); Greek: σάββατον (sabbaton)
translationNotes.note: The seventh day, set apart by God's command (Exodus 20:8-11). All work ceased from sunset Friday to sunset Saturday. By Jesus' day, rabbinical tradition had elaborated 39 categories of forbidden labor; many of Jesus' healings deliberately challenged those additional rules without violating the Torah command itself.

translationNotes.term: The one fast the law commands
translationNotes.original: Hebrew: לְעַנּוֹת נֶפֶשׁ (le-annoth nephesh, to afflict the soul)
translationNotes.note: 58:3 and 58:5 turn on a phrase from the law. The only fast the Torah requires is the Day of Atonement, where Leviticus 16:29-31 and 23:27-32 order you to afflict yourselves on the tenth day of the seventh month, and treat working that day as a capital matter. Every other fast in Israel was called for a crisis or taken on freely (Judges 20:26, Joel 1:14). 58:5 asks whether bowing the head like a reed is what afflicting yourself was ever supposed to mean.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: גֹּדֵר פֶּרֶץ (goder perets)
translationNotes.note: A perets is the gap an attacker knocks in a city wall, and until it is walled up the whole city is open. 58:12 gives the title to the people who do what 58:6-7 lists, and pairs it with restorer of streets to live in. Nehemiah 4 and 6 are the same work done literally, closing gaps in Jerusalem's wall while under threat.

stories.keyTakeaway: Isaiah rebukes the people for their hollow fasting and religious performance while ignoring injustice and oppression; true fasting means freeing the oppressed, feeding the hungry, and clothing the poor, which will bring restoration and God's favor.

stories.title: 🕯️ Isaiah 59
summaryBullets: Surely the arm of the LORD is not too short to save, nor His ear too dull to hear. (59:1).
But your iniquities have built barriers between you and your God, and your sins have hidden His face from you, so that He does not hear. (59:2).
For your hands are stained with blood, and your fingers with iniquity; your lips have spoken lies, and your tongue mutters injustice. (59:3).
No one calls for justice; no one pleads his case honestly. They rely on empty pleas; they tell lies; they conceive mischief and give birth to iniquity. (59:4).
