They hatch the eggs of vipers and weave a spider’s web. Whoever eats their eggs will die; crack one open, and a viper is hatched. (59:5).
Their cobwebs cannot be made into clothing, and they cannot cover themselves with their works. Their deeds are sinful deeds, and acts of violence are in their hands. (59:6).
Their feet run to evil; they are swift to shed innocent blood. Their thoughts are sinful thoughts; ruin and destruction lie in their wake. (59:7).
The way of peace they have not known, and there is no justice in their tracks. They have turned them into crooked paths; no one who treads on them will know peace. (59:8).
Therefore justice is far from us, and righteousness does not reach us. We hope for light, but there is darkness; for brightness, but we walk in gloom. (59:9).
Like the blind, we feel our way along the wall, groping like those without eyes. We stumble at midday as in the twilight; among the vigorous we are like the dead. (59:10).
We all growl like bears and moan like doves. We hope for justice, but find none, for salvation, but it is far from us. (59:11).
For our transgressions are multiplied before You, and our sins testify against us. Our transgressions are indeed with us, and we know our iniquities: (59:12).
rebelling and denying the LORD, turning away from our God, speaking oppression and revolt, conceiving and uttering lies from the heart. (59:13).
So justice is turned away, and righteousness stands at a distance. For truth has stumbled in the public square, and honesty cannot enter. (59:14).
Truth is missing, and whoever turns from evil becomes prey. The LORD looked and was displeased that there was no justice. (59:15).
He saw that there was no man; He was amazed that there was no one to intercede. So His own arm brought salvation, and His own righteousness sustained Him. (59:16).
He put on righteousness like a breastplate, and the helmet of salvation on His head; He put on garments of vengeance and wrapped Himself in a cloak of zeal. (59:17).
So He will repay according to their deeds: fury to His enemies, retribution to His foes, and recompense to the islands. (59:18).
So shall they fear the name of the LORD where the sun sets, and His glory where it rises. For He will come like a raging flood, driven by the breath of the LORD. (59:19).
“The Redeemer will come to Zion, to those in Jacob who turn from transgression,” declares the LORD. (59:20).

“As for Me, this is My covenant with them,” says the LORD. “My Spirit will not depart from you, and My words that I have put in your mouth will not depart from your mouth or from the mouths of your children and grandchildren, from now on and forevermore,” says the LORD. (59:21).
crossRefs: Romans 3:15-17: Paul quotes Isaiah 59:7-8: their feet are swift to shed blood, ruin and misery lie in their wake, and they have not known the way of peace.
Romans 11:26-27: Paul quotes Isaiah 59:20-21: 'The Deliverer will come from Zion; He will remove godlessness from Jacob.'
Ephesians 6:14-17: The breastplate of righteousness and the helmet of salvation, the armor Isaiah 59:17 puts on God Himself.
Deuteronomy 28:29: A covenant curse of groping about at noon like a blind man in the darkness, never prospering in your ways.
Isaiah 1:15: The same charge opens the book: God hides His eyes from their prayers because their hands are covered with blood.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: גֹּאֵל (goʾel), Greek (LXX): ῥυόμενος/λυτρωτής, Aramaic: פָרִיקָא/גואל
translationNotes.note: Kinsman-rescuer title now used for God’s saving arrival (59:20).

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: צְדָקָה כַּשִּׁרְיָן (righteousness as breastplate), Greek (LXX): θώραξ δικαιοσύνης, Aramaic: שִׁרְיָא דִּזַכָּוָתָא
translationNotes.note: Divine warrior gear (59:17), echoed later in Ephesians 6.

translationNotes.term: Adders' eggs and a spider's web
translationNotes.original: Hebrew: קוּרֵי עַכָּבִישׁ (qure akkavish, spider threads)
translationNotes.note: 59:5-6 gives two products and says what each is worth. Eat one of the eggs and it kills you, crush one and a viper comes out, so the thing is lethal either way. The web is the opposite kind of failure: 59:6 says their webs will not serve as clothing, and nobody covers themselves with what they have made. One is dangerous and one is useless.

translationNotes.term: Truth stumbles in the public square
translationNotes.original: Hebrew: רְחוֹב (rechov, the open square)
translationNotes.note: The rechov was the broad open space just inside the city gate, where cases were heard, contracts witnessed and business done in front of everyone; Ruth 4:1-11 shows a legal matter settled there with ten elders sitting in. 59:14 says justice is driven back and truth has fallen down in that exact place, which puts the collapse in the one spot the whole system depended on being sound.

stories.keyTakeaway: Isaiah catalogs widespread injustice and violence among the people, then describes the Lord putting on armor and achieving salvation himself because no one else will intervene; he promises the Redeemer will come to repentant Jacob and his Spirit will remain on them forever.

stories.title: 🌅 Isaiah 60
summaryBullets: Arise, shine, for your light has come, and the glory of the LORD rises upon you. (60:1).
For behold, darkness covers the earth, and thick darkness is over the peoples; but the LORD will rise upon you, and His glory will appear over you. (60:2).
Nations will come to your light, and kings to the brightness of your dawn. (60:3).
Lift up your eyes and look around: They all gather and come to you; your sons will come from afar, and your daughters will be carried on the arm. (60:4).
Then you will look and be radiant, and your heart will tremble and swell with joy, because the riches of the sea will be brought to you, and the wealth of the nations will come to you. (60:5).
Caravans of camels will cover your land, young camels of Midian and Ephah, and all from Sheba will come, bearing gold and frankincense and proclaiming the praises of the LORD. (60:6).
All the flocks of Kedar will be gathered to you; the rams of Nebaioth will serve you and go up on My altar with acceptance; I will adorn My glorious house. (60:7).
Who are these who fly like clouds, like doves to their shelters? (60:8).

Surely the islands will wait for Me, with the ships of Tarshish in the lead, to bring your children from afar, with their silver and gold, to the honor of the LORD your God, the Holy One of Israel, for He has glorified you. (60:9).
Foreigners will rebuild your walls, and their kings will serve you. Although I struck you in anger, yet in favor I will show you mercy. (60:10).
Your gates will always stand open; they will never be shut, day or night, so that the wealth of the nations may be brought into you, with their kings being led in procession. (60:11).
For the nation or kingdom that will not serve you will perish; it will be utterly destroyed. (60:12).
The glory of Lebanon will come to you— its cypress, elm, and boxwood together— to adorn the place of My sanctuary, and I will glorify the place of My feet. (60:13).
The sons of your oppressors will come and bow down to you; all who reviled you will fall facedown at your feet and call you the City of the LORD, Zion of the Holy One of Israel. (60:14).
Whereas you have been forsaken and despised, with no one passing through, I will make you an everlasting pride, a joy from age to age. (60:15).
You will drink the milk of nations and nurse at the breasts of royalty; you will know that I, the LORD, am your Savior and your Redeemer, the Mighty One of Jacob. (60:16).

Instead of bronze I will bring you gold; I will bring silver in place of iron, bronze instead of wood, and iron instead of stones. I will appoint peace as your governor and righteousness as your ruler. (60:17).
No longer will violence be heard in your land, nor ruin or destruction within your borders. But you will name your walls Salvation and your gates Praise. (60:18).
No longer will the sun be your light by day, nor the brightness of the moon shine on your night; for the LORD will be your everlasting light, and your God will be your splendor. (60:19).
Your sun will no longer set, and your moon will not wane; for the LORD will be your everlasting light, and the days of your sorrow will cease. (60:20).
Then all your people will be righteous; they will possess the land forever; they are the branch of My planting, the work of My hands, so that I may be glorified. (60:21).
The least of you will become a thousand, and the smallest a mighty nation. I am the LORD; in its time I will accomplish it quickly. (60:22).
crossRefs: Revelation 21:23-26: The city needs no sun or moon, the nations walk by its light, and the kings of the earth bring their glory into it.
Matthew 2:11: The Magi open their treasures and present the child with gold, frankincense, and myrrh.
1 Kings 10:1-2: The queen of Sheba arrives in Jerusalem with a caravan of camels bearing spices, gold in great abundance, and precious stones.
Psalm 72:10-11: The kings of Tarshish and distant shores bring tribute, the kings of Sheba and Seba offer gifts, and all kings bow down.
Haggai 2:7-9: The LORD shakes the nations, they come with their treasures, and He fills the house with glory greater than the former.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: קוּמִי אוֹרִי (qūmī ʾorī), Greek (LXX): φῶς φώτισαι, Aramaic: קוּמִי אֲנְהָרִי
translationNotes.note: Call to display God’s given glory (60:1).

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: לְבוֹנָה (levonah); Greek: λίβανος (libanos)
translationNotes.note: A milky-white resin from the Boswellia tree of southern Arabia. Burned as incense in the temple (Exodus 30:34); offered with every grain offering. The magi's second gift, traditionally read as signaling priesthood.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: שְׁבָא (Sheva) - מִדְיָן (Midyan) - קֵדָר (Qedar) - נְבָיוֹת (Nevayoth)
translationNotes.note: 60:6-7 is the caravan trade arriving as tribute. Sheba lay in southwest Arabia, in what is now Yemen, and controlled the incense route; its queen came up that road at 1 Kings 10:1-2 with camels carrying spices, gold and stones. Midian and Ephah were northwest Arabian, Kedar and Nebaioth were sons of Ishmael (Genesis 25:13). The goods named, gold and frankincense and flocks, are exactly what those peoples had to trade.

translationNotes.term: Your gates shall never be shut
translationNotes.original: Hebrew: וּפִתְּחוּ שְׁעָרַיִךְ תָּמִיד (u-phittechu she'arayikh tamid)
translationNotes.note: Every walled city shut its gates at dark and opened them at dawn, without exception, because the gate was the one weak point in the defence; Joshua 2:5 and Nehemiah 7:3 both turn on the closing hour. 60:11 says these stand open day and night, and gives the reason, so that wealth can be brought in. A gate that never closes is a statement that there is nothing left to keep out.

stories.keyTakeaway: Jerusalem is called to rise as nations and kings come to her light, bringing wealth and tribute; foreigners rebuild her walls while the Lord transforms her devastation into eternal splendor and peace.

stories.title: 🌅 Isaiah 61
summaryBullets: The Spirit of the Lord GOD is on Me, because the LORD has anointed Me to preach good news to the poor. He has sent Me to bind up the brokenhearted, to proclaim liberty to the captives and freedom to the prisoners, (61:1).
to proclaim the year of the LORD’s favor and the day of our God’s vengeance, to comfort all who mourn, (61:2).

to console the mourners in Zion — to give them a crown of beauty for ashes, the oil of joy for mourning, and a garment of praise for a spirit of despair. So they will be called oaks of righteousness, the planting of the LORD, that He may be glorified. (61:3).
They will rebuild the ancient ruins; they will restore the places long devastated; they will renew the ruined cities, the desolations of many generations. (61:4).
Strangers will stand and feed your flocks, and foreigners will be your plowmen and vinedressers. (61:5).
But you will be called the priests of the LORD; they will speak of you as ministers of our God; you will feed on the wealth of nations, and you will boast in their riches. (61:6).

Instead of shame, My people will have a double portion, and instead of humiliation, they will rejoice in their share; and so they will inherit a double portion in their land, and everlasting joy will be theirs. (61:7).
For I, the LORD, love justice; I hate robbery and iniquity; in My faithfulness I will give them their recompense and make an everlasting covenant with them. (61:8).
Their descendants will be known among the nations, and their offspring among the peoples. All who see them will acknowledge that they are a people the LORD has blessed. (61:9).

I will rejoice greatly in the LORD, my soul will exult in my God; for He has clothed me with garments of salvation and wrapped me in a robe of righteousness, as a bridegroom wears a priestly headdress, as a bride adorns herself with her jewels. (61:10).
For as the earth brings forth its growth, and as a garden enables seed to spring up, so the Lord GOD will cause righteousness and praise to spring up before all the nations. (61:11).
crossRefs: Luke 4:16-21: In the Nazareth synagogue Jesus reads Isaiah 61:1-2, stops at the year of the LORD's favor, and says the Scripture is fulfilled that day.
Leviticus 25:8-13: In the fiftieth year the horn sounds on the Day of Atonement, liberty is proclaimed in the land, and every man returns to his property.
Deuteronomy 21:17: The firstborn receives a double portion of everything his father has, the share Isaiah 61:7 promises the people.
Exodus 19:5-6: Israel is told they will be a kingdom of priests and a holy nation if they keep the covenant.
Matthew 11:5: Jesus lists the signs for John, ending with the good news preached to the poor.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: מָשַׁח (mashach) / רוּחַ אֲדֹנָי, Greek (LXX): ἔχρισέν με / πνεῦμα Κυρίου, Aramaic: מְשַׁח יָתִי / רוּחַ יוי
translationNotes.note: Authorization for the good-news proclamation (61:1).

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: יוֹבֵל (yobel)
translationNotes.note: Every 50th year, after seven sabbatical-year cycles (Leviticus 25). Land returned to original families, Hebrew slaves were freed, and debts cancelled; a structural reset of social and economic inequality. The 'year of the Lord's favor' Jesus proclaims in Luke 4:19 draws directly on jubilee language from Isaiah 61.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: פְּאֵר תַּחַת אֵפֶר (pe'er tachath epher)
translationNotes.note: 61:3 is a pun made of three letters rearranged. Epher is ashes, which a mourner poured on the head: Tamar does it at 2 Samuel 13:19 and Job's friends at Job 2:12. Pe'er is a wrapped headdress, the ornamental turban a bridegroom wears at 61:10 and part of the priests' dress at Exodus 39:28. The two words sound almost identical in Hebrew, and the line swaps one for the other on the same head.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: אֵילֵי הַצֶּדֶק (ele ha-tsedeq, terebinths of righteousness)
translationNotes.note: 61:3 ends by calling them the planting of the LORD, and the tree named is the terebinth or great oak, the long-lived landmark tree of the region that outlasts generations and marks a place. Abraham camps by the oaks of Mamre (Genesis 13:18) and Deborah is buried under one (Genesis 35:8). Isaiah had used the same tree at 1:30 for a people whose leaves were fading.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: מִשְׁנֶה (mishneh, double)
translationNotes.note: 61:7 promises a double share instead of shame, and the phrase comes from inheritance law. Deuteronomy 21:17 requires a father to give the firstborn a double portion of everything he has, whether he favours that son's mother or not. The chapter is handing the eldest son's share to people who had been dispossessed.

stories.keyTakeaway: The speaker, anointed by God's Spirit, announces good news to the poor, freedom for captives, and comfort for mourners; God promises to rebuild ruins, restore cities, and establish an everlasting covenant with his people. Righteousness and praise will flourish before all nations as the Lord's people inherit blessing and joy.

headings.text: The Year of the Lord’s Favor

stories.title: 🌅 Isaiah 62
summaryBullets: For Zion’s sake I will not keep silent, and for Jerusalem’s sake I will not keep still, until her righteousness shines like a bright light, her salvation like a blazing torch. (62:1).
Nations will see your righteousness, and all kings your glory. You will be called by a new name that the mouth of the LORD will bestow. (62:2).
You will be a crown of glory in the hand of the LORD, a royal diadem in the palm of your God. (62:3).

No longer will you be called Forsaken, nor your land named Desolate; but you will be called Hephzibah, and your land Beulah; for the LORD will take delight in you, and your land will be His bride. (62:4).
For as a young man marries a young woman, so your sons will marry you; and as a bridegroom rejoices over his bride, so your God will rejoice over you. (62:5).
On your walls, O Jerusalem, I have posted watchmen; they will never be silent day or night. You who call on the LORD shall take no rest for yourselves, (62:6).
nor give Him any rest until He establishes Jerusalem and makes her the praise of the earth. (62:7).
The LORD has sworn by His right hand and by His mighty arm: “Never again will I give your grain to your enemies for food, nor will foreigners drink the new wine for which you have toiled. (62:8).
For those who harvest grain will eat it and praise the LORD, and those who gather grapes will drink the wine in My holy courts.” (62:9).
Go out, go out through the gates; prepare the way for the people! Build it up, build up the highway; clear away the stones; raise a banner for the nations! (62:10).
Behold, the LORD has proclaimed to the ends of the earth, “Say to Daughter Zion: See, your Savior comes! Look, His reward is with Him, and His recompense goes before Him.” (62:11).
And they will be called the Holy People, the Redeemed of The LORD; and you will be called Sought Out, A City Not Forsaken. (62:12).
crossRefs: Matthew 21:5: The entry into Jerusalem is announced with the words, 'Say to the Daughter of Zion, See, your King comes to you.'
2 Kings 21:1: Hephzibah, the new name given to Zion in Isaiah 62:4, was the name of Hezekiah's wife and Manasseh's mother.
Hosea 2:19-20: 'I will betroth you to Me forever; I will betroth you in righteousness and justice, in loving devotion and compassion.'
Ezekiel 33:6-7: The watchman who sees the sword coming and fails to blow the horn is held accountable for the life it takes.
Deuteronomy 28:30-33: A covenant curse that a people you do not know will eat the produce of your land, which Isaiah 62:8-9 reverses.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: חֶפְצִי־בָהּ (‘My Delight Is in Her’) / בְּעוּלָה (‘Married’), Greek (LXX): Θελητή / Γαμητή, Aramaic: חֵפְצִי בַּהּ / תְּבוּלָא
translationNotes.note: Names signal God’s delight and restored bond (62:4).

translationNotes.term: A crown in the hand of the LORD
translationNotes.original: Hebrew: עֲטֶרֶת תִּפְאֶרֶת (atereth tiph'ereth, a crown of beauty)
translationNotes.note: 62:3 puts the crown in the hand rather than on a head, which is where a crown is held while it is being looked at or before it is given. A royal diadem was the single object that carried a kingdom's standing, taken off a defeated king and put on the victor (2 Samuel 12:30). The verse leaves it held out, in the hand of God, not worn by anyone.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: הַמַּזְכִּרִים (ha-mazkirim, those who bring to remembrance)
translationNotes.note: 62:6 posts watchmen who never keep silent, day or night, and the word for them is drawn from the court: a mazkir was the royal official who kept the record and brought matters before the king (2 Samuel 8:16). So the picture combines two jobs, the sentry on the wall who calls out what he sees, and the recorder who will not let a case drop. 62:7 tells them to give God no rest until Jerusalem is established.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: סֹלּוּ סֹלּוּ הַמְסִלָּה סַקְּלוּ מֵאֶבֶן (sollu sollu ha-mesillah saqqelu me-even)
translationNotes.note: 62:10 is road work. When a king was coming, crews went out ahead to build up the roadbed, level the surface and throw the loose stones off it, because a route through that country was a track over rock unless somebody made it otherwise. The verb saqal normally means to stone someone; here it means to de-stone the road. 40:3 gives the same order and 57:14 repeats it.

stories.keyTakeaway: The prophet announces God's commitment to Jerusalem's vindication; the nation will be renamed, restored, and married to God like a bridegroom to a bride, with watchmen posted on its walls and a proclamation sent to the earth that a Savior comes with reward.

stories.title: 🩸 Isaiah 63
summaryBullets: Who is this coming from Edom, from Bozrah with crimson-stained garments? Who is this robed in splendor, marching in the greatness of His strength? “It is I, proclaiming vindication, mighty to save.” (63:1).
Why are Your clothes red, and Your garments like one who treads the winepress? (63:2).

“I have trodden the winepress alone, and no one from the nations was with Me. I trampled them in My anger and trod them down in My fury; their blood spattered My garments, and all My clothes were stained. (63:3).
For the day of vengeance was in My heart, and the year of My redemption had come. (63:4).
I looked, but there was no one to help; I was appalled that no one assisted. So My arm brought Me salvation, and My own wrath upheld Me. (63:5).
I trampled the nations in My anger; in My wrath I made them drunk and poured out their blood on the ground.” (63:6).

I will make known the LORD’s loving devotion and His praiseworthy acts, because of all that the LORD has done for us— the many good things for the house of Israel according to His great compassion and loving devotion. (63:7).
For He said, “They are surely My people, sons who will not be disloyal.” So He became their Savior. (63:8).
In all their distress, He too was afflicted, and the Angel of His Presence saved them. In His love and compassion He redeemed them; He lifted them up and carried them all the days of old. (63:9).
But they rebelled and grieved His Holy Spirit. So He turned and became their enemy, and He Himself fought against them. (63:10).

Then His people remembered the days of old, the days of Moses. Where is He who brought them through the sea with the shepherds of His flock? Where is the One who set His Holy Spirit among them, (63:11).
who sent His glorious arm to lead them by the right hand of Moses, who divided the waters before them to gain for Himself everlasting renown, (63:12).
who led them through the depths like a horse in the wilderness, so that they did not stumble? (63:13).
Like cattle going down to the valley, the Spirit of the LORD gave them rest. You led Your people this way to make for Yourself a glorious name. (63:14).
Look down from heaven and see, from Your holy and glorious habitation. Where are Your zeal and might? Your yearning and compassion for me are restrained. (63:15).
Yet You are our Father, though Abraham does not know us and Israel does not acknowledge us. You, O LORD, are our Father; our Redeemer from Everlasting is Your name. (63:16).
Why, O LORD, do You make us stray from Your ways and harden our hearts from fearing You? Return, for the sake of Your servants, the tribes of Your heritage. (63:17).
For a short while Your people possessed Your holy place, but our enemies have trampled Your sanctuary. (63:18).
We have become like those You never ruled, like those not called by Your name. (63:19).
crossRefs: Revelation 19:13-15: He is dressed in a robe dipped in blood, and He treads the winepress of the fury of the wrath of God.
Revelation 14:19-20: The grapes of the earth are thrown into the great winepress of God's wrath and trodden outside the city.
Isaiah 34:5-6: The sword of the LORD comes down on Edom, and He has a sacrifice in Bozrah, the same two names that open this chapter.
Exodus 33:14-15: 'My Presence will go with you,' says the LORD, and Moses refuses to move without it.
Ephesians 4:30: 'Do not grieve the Holy Spirit of God, in whom you were sealed for the day of redemption.'

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: אֱדוֹם (Edom) - Hebrew: בָּצְרָה (Botsrah)
translationNotes.note: Edom is the nation descended from Esau (Genesis 36:1, 8), holding the rugged highlands south-east of the Dead Sea, and Bozrah was its chief town on that plateau in what is now southern Jordan. The grudge is old: Edom refused Israel passage on the way up from Egypt (Numbers 20:14-21), and Obadiah 1:10-14 and Psalm 137:7 charge Edom with standing at the crossroads cutting down escapees the day Jerusalem fell.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: פּוּרָה (purah) - Hebrew: גַּת (gat)
translationNotes.note: A winepress was cut into bedrock: a shallow upper floor where men trod the grapes barefoot, holding ropes or a rail for balance, and a channel running the juice down into a lower collecting vat. The juice splashed the treader red to the knee and stained his clothes. Treading was normally the loudest, most cheerful work of the year, with shouting and song (Isaiah 16:10; Jeremiah 48:33), which is what makes the one man treading alone here so terrible.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: שְׁנַת גְּאוּלַי (shenat geulai)
translationNotes.note: Geulah is family law, not sentiment. The go'el, the nearest kinsman, was obliged to buy back land the family had lost, to redeem a relative who had sold himself into service, and to pursue a killer as avenger of blood (Leviticus 25:25, 47-49; Numbers 35:19; Ruth 4:1-10). Verse 4 pairs the day of vengeance and the year of the redeemed because both belong to the same office.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: מַלְאַךְ פָּנָיו (malakh panav)
translationNotes.note: Literally the messenger of His face. Malakh means a sent one, whether human or heavenly. The exodus account is what verse 9 is pointing at: Exodus 23:20-21 sends an angel before Israel with the warning that God's name is in him, and Exodus 33:14-15 has Moses refusing to move unless God's own presence, His face, goes with them.

translationNotes.term: Our enemies have trampled Your sanctuary
translationNotes.original: Hebrew: מִקְדָּשׁ (miqdash)
translationNotes.note: The sanctuary is Solomon's temple in Jerusalem. 2 Kings 25:8-9 dates its end: in the nineteenth year of Nebuchadnezzar, Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard burned the house of the LORD, the palace, and every great house in the city, and the walls were pulled down. Verse 18 is a prayer prayed on the other side of that.

stories.keyTakeaway: A figure arrives from Edom with blood-stained garments, declaring he has trampled nations alone in his anger and achieved salvation by his own arm; the speaker then recalls the Lord's past kindnesses to Israel, their rebellion against his Spirit, and pleads for him to return and restore his people from their enemies.

stories.title: 🩸 Isaiah 64
summaryBullets: If only You would rend the heavens and come down, so that mountains would quake at Your presence, (64:1).
as fire kindles the brushwood and causes the water to boil, to make Your name known to Your enemies, so that the nations will tremble at Your presence! (64:2).
When You did awesome works that we did not expect, You came down, and the mountains trembled at Your presence. (64:3).
From ancient times no one has heard, no ear has perceived, no eye has seen any God besides You, who acts on behalf of those who wait for Him. (64:4).
You welcome those who gladly do right, who remember Your ways. Surely You were angry, for we sinned. How can we be saved if we remain in our sins? (64:5).
Each of us has become like something unclean, and all our righteous acts are like filthy rags; we all wither like a leaf, and our iniquities carry us away like the wind. (64:6).
No one calls on Your name or strives to take hold of You. For You have hidden Your face from us and delivered us into the hand of our iniquity. (64:7).
But now, O LORD, You are our Father; we are the clay, and You are the potter; we are all the work of Your hand. (64:8).
Do not be angry, O LORD, beyond measure; do not remember our iniquity forever. Oh, look upon us, we pray; we are all Your people! (64:9).
Your holy cities have become a wilderness. Zion has become a wasteland and Jerusalem a desolation. (64:10).
Our holy and beautiful temple, where our fathers praised You, has been burned with fire, and all that was dear to us lies in ruins. (64:11).
After all this, O LORD, will You restrain Yourself? Will You keep silent and afflict us beyond measure? (64:12).
crossRefs: 1 Corinthians 2:9: Paul quotes Isaiah 64:4: no eye has seen, no ear has heard, what God has prepared for those who love Him.
Exodus 19:16-19: Sinai is wrapped in smoke because the LORD descends on it in fire, and the whole mountain trembles violently.
Judges 5:4-5: In Deborah's song the earth trembles and the mountains quake before the LORD, the One of Sinai.
Jeremiah 18:1-6: The LORD sends Jeremiah to the potter's house and says Israel is clay in His hand as the clay is in the potter's.
2 Kings 25:9: Nebuchadnezzar's captain burns the house of the LORD, the royal palace, and every significant building in Jerusalem.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: פוּרָה / גַּת (purah/gat), Greek (LXX): ληνός, Aramaic: מַעְצְרָא
translationNotes.note: Crushing imagery for judgment (63:2-3).

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: בֶּגֶד עִדִּים (beged ʿiddim), Greek (LXX): ῥάκος ἀποκαθημένης, Aramaic: לְבוּשׁ מְסוּא
translationNotes.note: Strong image of ritual uncleanness for human righteousness (64:6).

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: קָרַעְתָּ שָׁמַיִם (qaraʿta shamayim), Greek (LXX): διέρρηξας οὐρανούς, Aramaic: קְרַע שְׁמַיָּא
translationNotes.note: Prayer for a visible, seismic intervention (64:1).

stories.keyTakeaway: The people implore God to come down and reveal himself as he once did, acknowledging their sin and uncleanness; they lament that their sacred cities and temple lie in ruins and plead with him not to abandon them forever.

stories.title: 🌍 Isaiah 65
summaryBullets: “I revealed Myself to those who did not ask for Me; I was found by those who did not seek Me. To a nation that did not call My name, I said, ‘Here I am! Here I am!’ (65:1).
All day long I have held out My hands to an obstinate people who walk in the wrong path, who follow their own imaginations, (65:2).
to a people who continually provoke Me to My face, sacrificing in the gardens and burning incense on altars of brick, (65:3).
sitting among the graves, spending nights in secret places, eating the meat of pigs and polluted broth from their bowls. (65:4).
They say, ‘Keep to yourself; do not come near me, for I am holier than you!’ Such people are smoke in My nostrils, a fire that burns all day long. (65:5).
Behold, it is written before Me: I will not keep silent, but I will repay; I will pay it back into their laps, (65:6).

both for your iniquities and for those of your fathers,” says the LORD. “Because they burned incense on the mountains and scorned Me on the hills, I will measure into their laps full payment for their former deeds.” (65:7).

This is what the LORD says: “As the new wine is found in a cluster of grapes, and men say, ‘Do not destroy it, for it contains a blessing,’ so I will act on behalf of My servants; I will not destroy them all. (65:8).
And I will bring forth descendants from Jacob, and heirs from Judah; My elect will possess My mountains, and My servants will dwell there. (65:9).
Sharon will become a pasture for flocks, and the Valley of Achor a resting place for herds, for My people who seek Me. (65:10).
But you who forsake the LORD, who forget My holy mountain, who set a table for Fortune and fill bowls of mixed wine for Destiny, (65:11).

I will destine you for the sword, and you will all kneel down to be slaughtered, because I called and you did not answer, I spoke and you did not listen; you did evil in My sight and chose that in which I did not delight.” (65:12).

Therefore this is what the Lord GOD says: “My servants will eat, but you will go hungry; My servants will drink, but you will go thirsty; My servants will rejoice, but you will be put to shame. (65:13).
My servants will shout for joy with a glad heart, but you will cry out with a heavy heart and wail with a broken spirit. (65:14).
You will leave behind your name as a curse for My chosen ones, and the Lord GOD will slay you; but to His servants He will give another name. (65:15).

Whoever invokes a blessing in the land will do so by the God of truth, and whoever takes an oath in the land will swear by the God of truth. For the former troubles will be forgotten and hidden from My sight. (65:16).
For behold, I will create new heavens and a new earth. The former things will not be remembered, nor will they come to mind. (65:17).
But be glad and rejoice forever in what I create; for I will create Jerusalem to be a joy and its people to be a delight. (65:18).
I will rejoice in Jerusalem and take delight in My people. The sounds of weeping and crying will no longer be heard in her. (65:19).

No longer will a nursing infant live but a few days, or an old man fail to live out his years. For the youth will die at a hundred years, and he who fails to reach a hundred will be considered accursed. (65:20).
They will build houses and dwell in them; they will plant vineyards and eat their fruit. (65:21).

No longer will they build houses for others to inhabit, nor plant for others to eat. For as is the lifetime of a tree, so will be the days of My people, and My chosen ones will fully enjoy the work of their hands. (65:22).
They will not labor in vain or bear children doomed to disaster; for they will be a people blessed by the LORD — they and their descendants with them. (65:23).
Even before they call, I will answer, and while they are still speaking, I will hear. (65:24).

The wolf and the lamb will feed together, and the lion will eat straw like the ox, but the food of the serpent will be dust. They will neither harm nor destroy on all My holy mountain,” says the LORD. (65:25).
crossRefs: Romans 10:20-21: Paul quotes Isaiah 65:1-2: 'I was found by those who did not seek Me,' and 'All day long I have held out My hands.'
Leviticus 11:7: The pig has a split hoof but does not chew the cud, so it is unclean for Israel and may not be eaten.
Deuteronomy 18:10-11: Consulting a medium or a spiritist, or inquiring of the dead, is forbidden, the practice behind sitting among the graves.
Revelation 21:1-4: John sees a new heaven and a new earth, and God wipes away every tear from their eyes.
Isaiah 11:6-9: The wolf lies down with the lamb, the lion eats straw like the ox, and nothing harms or destroys on the holy mountain.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: בּוֹרֵא (boreʾ), Greek (LXX): κτίζω, Aramaic: בָּרֵא
translationNotes.note: Same creation verb used for God’s original making (65:17).

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: גַּד (Gad) - מְנִי (Meni)
translationNotes.note: 65:11 has them setting a table and filling mixed wine for two gods, and English prints the meanings of the names instead of the names. Gad means fortune and Meni means what is allotted, and both were worshipped in the region; Gad's name survives in place names such as Baal-gad (Joshua 11:17). The practice described is a meal laid out for a deity, a table set and wine poured, done for luck.

translationNotes.term: Sitting among the graves, eating swine's flesh
translationNotes.original: Hebrew: בַּקְּבָרִים (ba-qevarim, in the tombs) - בְּשַׂר הַחֲזִיר (besar ha-chazir)
translationNotes.note: 65:4 puts two forbidden things in one line. Spending the night among tombs was how the dead were consulted for answers, which Deuteronomy 18:11 bans by name, and contact with a corpse or a grave made a person unclean for seven days (Numbers 19:16). Pork is forbidden at Leviticus 11:7 and Deuteronomy 14:8. 65:4 is describing worship carried out deliberately in the two places the law shut off.

translationNotes.term: They shall not build and another inhabit
translationNotes.original: Hebrew: לֹא יִבְנוּ וְאַחֵר יֵשֵׁב (lo yivnu ve-acher yeshev)
translationNotes.note: 65:21-22 is a covenant curse read backwards. Deuteronomy 28:30 threatens exactly this as punishment: you will build a house and not live in it, plant a vineyard and not enjoy its fruit, because an enemy takes it. 65:22 cancels each clause in the same order and adds the days of a tree to the measure of their days.

translationNotes.term: Dust shall be the serpent's food
translationNotes.original: Hebrew: וְנָחָשׁ עָפָר לַחְמוֹ (ve-nachash aphar lachmo)
translationNotes.note: 65:25 gathers the wolf and lamb and the lion and ox from 11:6-9 into one line, and then adds a clause that is not in the earlier passage. Dust as the serpent's food is the sentence passed at Genesis 3:14, quoted here word for word. Everything else in the verse is changed; that one stands.

stories.keyTakeaway: God made himself available to those who rejected him and will punish the disobedient with the sword; but he will preserve a remnant of servants from Jacob and Judah, and will create new heavens and a new earth where his chosen people dwell in peace, long life, and abundance without sorrow or harm.

headings.text: A New Heaven and a New Earth

stories.title: 🌍 Isaiah 66
summaryBullets: This is what the LORD says: “Heaven is My throne, and earth is My footstool. What kind of house will you build for Me? Or where will My place of repose be? (66:1).
Has not My hand made all these things? And so they came into being,” declares the LORD. “This is the one I will esteem: he who is humble and contrite in spirit, who trembles at My word. (66:2).

Whoever slaughters an ox is like one who slays a man; whoever sacrifices a lamb is like one who breaks a dog’s neck; whoever presents a grain offering is like one who offers pig’s blood; whoever offers frankincense is like one who blesses an idol. Indeed, they have chosen their own ways and delighted in their abominations. (66:3).

So I will choose their punishment and I will bring terror upon them, because I called and no one answered, I spoke and no one listened. But they did evil in My sight and chose that in which I did not delight.” (66:4).

You who tremble at His word, hear the word of the LORD: “Your brothers who hate you and exclude you because of My name have said, ‘Let the LORD be glorified that we may see your joy!’ But they will be put to shame.” (66:5).
Hear the uproar from the city; listen to the voice from the temple! It is the voice of the LORD, repaying His enemies what they deserve! (66:6).
“Before she was in labor, she gave birth; before she was in pain, she delivered a boy. (66:7).

Who has heard of such as this? Who has seen such things? Can a country be born in a day or a nation be delivered in an instant? Yet as soon as Zion was in labor, she gave birth to her children. (66:8).
Shall I bring a baby to the point of birth and not deliver it?” says the LORD. “Or will I who deliver close the womb?” says your God. (66:9).
Be glad for Jerusalem and rejoice over her, all who love her. Rejoice greatly with her, all who mourn over her, (66:10).
so that you may nurse and be satisfied at her comforting breasts; you may drink deeply and delight yourselves in her glorious abundance. (66:11).

For this is what the LORD says: “I will extend peace to her like a river, and the wealth of nations like a flowing stream; you will nurse and be carried on her arm, and bounced upon her knees. (66:12).
As a mother comforts her son, so will I comfort you, and you will be consoled over Jerusalem.” (66:13).
When you see, you will rejoice, and you will flourish like grass; then the hand of the LORD will be revealed to His servants, but His wrath will be shown to His enemies. (66:14).
For behold, the LORD will come with fire— His chariots are like a whirlwind— to execute His anger with fury and His rebuke with flames of fire. (66:15).
For by fire and by His sword, the LORD will execute judgment on all flesh, and many will be slain by the LORD. (66:16).

“Those who consecrate and purify themselves to enter the groves — to follow one in the center of those who eat the flesh of swine and vermin and rats — will perish together,” declares the LORD. (66:17).
“And I, knowing their deeds and thoughts, am coming to gather all nations and tongues, and they will come and see My glory. (66:18).

I will establish a sign among them, and I will send survivors from among them to the nations — to Tarshish, Put, and the archers of Lud; to Tubal, Javan, and the islands far away who have not heard of My fame or seen My glory. So they will proclaim My glory among the nations. (66:19).

And they will bring all your brothers from all the nations as a gift to the LORD on horses and chariots and wagons, on mules and camels, to My holy mountain Jerusalem,” says the LORD, “just as the Israelites bring an offering in a clean vessel to the house of the LORD.” (66:20).
“And I will select some of them as priests and Levites,” says the LORD. (66:21).
“For just as the new heavens and the new earth, which I will make, will endure before Me,” declares the LORD, “so your descendants and your name will endure. (66:22).
From one New Moon to another and from one Sabbath to another, all mankind will come to worship before Me,” says the LORD. (66:23).

“As they go forth, they will see the corpses of the men who have rebelled against Me; for their worm will never die, their fire will never be quenched, and they will be a horror to all mankind.” (66:24).
crossRefs: Acts 7:49-50: Stephen quotes Isaiah 66:1-2 before the Sanhedrin: heaven is My throne and the earth is My footstool.
1 Kings 8:27: Solomon asks whether God will really dwell on earth, since the highest heavens cannot contain Him, much less this temple.
Mark 9:47-48: Jesus warns of the place where their worm never dies and the fire is never quenched, quoting Isaiah 66:24.
Malachi 1:11: 'My name will be great among the nations,' and in every place incense and pure offerings will be presented in His name.
Romans 15:16: Paul serves as a minister to the Gentiles so that they may become an offering acceptable to God, sanctified by the Holy Spirit.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: נֶכֶה־רוּחַ / חָרֵד עַל דְּבָרִי, Greek (LXX): ταπεινὸς τῷ πνεύματι / τρέμων τοὺς λόγους, Aramaic: מְכִיךְ רוּחָא / דְּחֵיל מִן פִּתְגָמִי
translationNotes.note: God’s chosen worship posture (66:2-5).

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: תּוֹלָעָתָם לֹא תָמוּת… אֵשָׁם לֹא תִכְבֶּה, Greek (LXX): ὁ σκώληξ οὐ τελευτᾷ… τὸ πῦρ οὐ σβέννυται, Aramaic: תַּלְעָא לָא מֵית… נוּרָא לָא דָעֵךְ
translationNotes.note: Unending sign of judgment against persistent rebellion (66:24).

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: שָׁחָה (shachah)
translationNotes.note: To bow down or prostrate oneself in humility. Used for reverence toward God (Genesis 22:5; Exodus 4:31; Psalm 95:6; Isaiah 66:23) but also for kings or angels. Very physical and posture-centered.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: שַׁבָּת (shabbat); Greek: σάββατον (sabbaton)
translationNotes.note: The seventh day, set apart by God's command (Exodus 20:8-11). All work ceased from sunset Friday to sunset Saturday. By Jesus' day, rabbinical tradition had elaborated 39 categories of forbidden labor; many of Jesus' healings deliberately challenged those additional rules without violating the Torah command itself.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: לְבוֹנָה (levonah); Greek: λίβανος (libanos)
translationNotes.note: A milky-white resin from the Boswellia tree of southern Arabia. Burned as incense in the temple (Exodus 30:34); offered with every grain offering. The magi's second gift, traditionally read as signaling priesthood.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: עֹרֵף כֶּלֶב (oreph kelev, breaking a dog's neck) - דַּם־חֲזִיר (dam chazir, pig's blood)
translationNotes.note: 66:3 pairs each lawful offering with something unthinkable: the ox with killing a man, the lamb with breaking a dog's neck, the grain offering with pig's blood, the incense with blessing an idol. Dogs were unclean scavengers, not pets, and breaking an animal's neck was how a firstborn donkey was destroyed if nobody redeemed it (Exodus 13:13). The verse does not say the offerings stopped; it says what they had become.

translationNotes.term: Tarshish, Pul, Lud, Tubal and Javan
translationNotes.original: Hebrew: תַּרְשִׁישׁ (Tarshish) - לוּד (Lud) - תֻּבַל (Tuval) - יָוָן (Yavan)
translationNotes.note: 66:19 sends survivors to named nations at the far edge of the known world. Javan is Greece, the name used for the Greeks at Genesis 10:2 and Daniel 8:21. Tubal lay in Anatolia, Lud in Asia Minor, and Tarshish was the far western port the long-haul ships sailed for, the direction Jonah ran. The point of the list is distance: these are the places that have never heard the report or seen the glory.

stories.keyTakeaway: The LORD declares that true worship requires humility and obedience rather than ritual sacrifices, and promises that those who tremble at his word will see Jerusalem restored and all nations gathered to his holy mountain. He will judge the rebellious with fire while the faithful enjoy his comfort and peace.

intro:
Isaiah was written by Isaiah son of Amoz (Isaiah 1:1), the prophet of Judah from the latter half of the 8th century BC through the early 7th century BC. His ministry spanned at least sixty years, during the reigns of four kings of Judah: Uzziah (792-740 BC), Jotham (750-732 BC), Ahaz (735-715 BC), and Hezekiah (715-686 BC); Jewish tradition extends his ministry into the early reign of Manasseh (697-642 BC). The book was composed during this period (c. 740-680 BC) in Jerusalem. Isaiah was the son of Amoz; Jewish tradition (Talmud Megillah 10b) holds that Amoz was the brother of King Amaziah of Judah, making Isaiah a cousin of King Uzziah and a member of the royal family with regular access to the throne room. (Amoz, Isaiah's father, written with the Hebrew letter tsade, is a different name from Amos the prophet, who lived a generation earlier.) Isaiah was married to a woman the text calls a prophetess (Isaiah 8:3) and had at least two sons with prophetic names: Shear-Jashub ("a remnant shall return," Isaiah 7:3) and Maher-shalal-hash-baz ("quick to plunder, swift to spoil," Isaiah 8:3). Jewish tradition (Talmud Yevamot 49b; the apocryphal Ascension of Isaiah) holds that Isaiah was martyred under King Manasseh by being sawn in two; Hebrews 11:37 ("they were sawn in two") is traditionally read as alluding to his death.

The historical setting is the rise of the Neo-Assyrian Empire to its dominant position over the ancient Near East. Tiglath-Pileser III (745-727 BC) had pioneered the Assyrian policy of conquest and forced deportation. The northern kingdom of Israel fell to Shalmaneser V and Sargon II in 722 BC, ending the line of northern kings and scattering the ten northern tribes. Sennacherib invaded Judah in 701 BC, capturing nearly every fortified city and besieging Jerusalem itself during the fourteenth year of Hezekiah (Isaiah 36-37; 2 Kings 18-19; 2 Chronicles 32; confirmed by Sennacherib's own Taylor Prism inscription, now in the British Museum). The Assyrians eventually withdrew after divine intervention, but Judah was reduced to a vassal state. Esarhaddon (681-669 BC) and Ashurbanipal (669-631 BC) continued Assyrian dominance into Manasseh's reign. Egypt under the 25th Dynasty (the Kushite or Ethiopian Pharaohs, including Taharqa, the biblical Tirhakah) was the only counterweight to Assyria in the region until its own conquest by Esarhaddon in 671 BC.

Isaiah is the twenty-third book of the Christian Old Testament and the first of the four Major Prophets (Isaiah, Jeremiah, Ezekiel, Daniel). The Hebrew name Yeshayahu (יְשַׁעְיָהוּ) means "Yahuah is salvation" or "Yahuah saves," combining the verbal root yasha ("to save") with the divine name Yah. The Great Isaiah Scroll (1QIsa-a), discovered at Qumran in 1947 and dated to around 125 BC, is one of the most famous of the Dead Sea Scrolls; it preserves the complete text of all 66 chapters of Isaiah on a 24-foot leather scroll and is more than a thousand years older than the previously oldest extant Hebrew manuscripts. A second, fragmentary Isaiah scroll (1QIsa-b) and additional Isaiah manuscripts from other Qumran caves confirm the remarkable stability of the Isaiah text across the centuries.
